**Surah 17: al-Isra' (The Night Journey)**

It is also called "Subhan" and "Bani Isra'il."

Its purpose is to turn wholly toward Allah, to strip away everything other than Him, because He alone is the Owner of the details of affairs and the One who grants some creatures preference over others. This is the practice of taqwa (God-consciousness), whose lowest degree is tawhid (affirmation of God's oneness), with which al-Nahl opens, and whose highest degree is ihsan (excellence in worship), with which it closes. Ihsan is the annihilation of the self from everything other than Allah.

It is among the earliest surahs revealed. al-Bukhari, in the Book of the Virtues of the Qur'an, and others narrate from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: "Bani Isra'il, al-Kahf, Maryam, Ta-Ha and al-Anbiya' are among the first noble ones, and they are part of my ancient treasure."

Each of its names clearly indicates what has been mentioned as its purpose. As for "Subhan," which is a proper noun for tanzih (declaring Allah free of imperfection), it is among the clearest indications of this purpose, because whoever is in the utmost purity from every deficiency is worthy that we worship none but Him and turn away from everything else, since He is characterized by what has been mentioned. As for "Bani Isra'il," whoever comprehends the details of their affairs, in their journey to the holy land, which resembles the night journey, and in the giving of the Book to them, along with what is mentioned about them in this surah, will know this.

*In the name of Allah* (the King, the Owner of all affairs), *the All-Merciful* (to all that He has brought into being, by nurturing it), *the Most Merciful* (to whoever He singles out for committing to acts that please Him).

Since the purpose of al-Nahl was tanazzuh (exalting Allah above deficiency) from haste and other attributes of imperfection, and the attainment of perfection, which yields the conclusion that He is capable of great matters, among them making the Hour like the blink of an eye or nearer, and since it concluded after praising Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and commanding that he be followed, by alluding to the victory of His allies (despite their weakness at that time and their small number) over His enemies (despite their multitude and strength), and this was among the breaking of customary habits and the exceptions to regular patterns, and since He commanded them to be patient and to do good, this surah opens by realizing what the conclusion had pointed to, through what He broke of habit in the night journey, and by declaring His noble self free from any suspicion that such a thing is improbable. This is to alert that He is capable of doing great and numerous, arduous matters in the shortest time, to repel what might be imagined, or what those who hear His prohibition of haste and His command to patience might raise as an objection, and to clarify that He is with the God-fearing and the good-doers, and to honor the affair of Muhammad (ﷺ), and to inform that he is the head of the good-doers and the highest in rank and the greatest in station, through what He gave him of special privileges, among them the praiseworthy station (al-maqam al-mahmud). It is also an illustration of what He reported about the matter of the Hour.

So He said (Exalted is He): ﴿Glory be to Him﴾. Subhan is a proper noun for tanzih, indicating its most eloquent meaning. It is in the accusative, governed by a verb that is omitted from expression and whose place this word fills. ﴿Who took His servant by night﴾. He declared His noble self free from every trace of deficiency that His enemies might attribute to Him, with this most eloquent word, following the command to patience at the end of al-Nahl, just as He declared His noble self free by that word following the prohibition of haste at its beginning. It also refutes what was known of their rejection of him and their denial of him when he told them of the night journey. Within it, there is also an allusion to wonder at this story, to alert that it is among matters so great that its description cannot be fully encompassed.

Since the preposition (harf al-jarr) is restricted to conveying transitivity in *sara* (which has the meaning of *asra*), and *asra* is used both transitively and intransitively, He expressed it with *asra*, and the intransitive form was chosen to indicate companionship, as an increase in honor. So He said (Exalted is He): ﴿with His servant﴾, meaning the one who is the most noble of His servants and the most deserving of being attributed to Him, who never worshipped anyone other than Him, neither an idol nor anything else, in hope of intercession or anything else.

Since the night journey is travel at night, and since a thing may be applied to part of its meaning by the implication of inclusion (dalalat al-tadammun), as a figurative usage (majaz mursal), He negated this with His saying (Exalted is He): ﴿by night﴾, and so that by the diminutive nunation (tanwin al-tahqir, the nunation that signifies smallness) it would indicate that this great matter took place in a small part of the night, and that he, peace be upon him, did not need, in the night journey, the ascent to the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha) and the hearing of speech from the Most High, to any discipline through fasting or otherwise, but was already prepared for that, fit for it. So He raised him from the lowest bed to the Throne.

﴿From the Sacred Mosque﴾, meaning from the Ka'bah, the honored, the mosque of Ibrahim, peace be upon him. It is said he was sleeping in al-Hatim, and it is said in al-Hijr, and it is said in the house of Umm Hani, and this last is the view of the majority. The mosque here therefore refers to the Haram, since it is the courtyard of the mosque. ﴿To the Farthest Mosque﴾, meaning the one that was then the farthest of the mosques, and the farthest of the two greatest mosques absolutely from Makkah, between them being forty nights. He led all the prophets in prayer there: Ibrahim, Musa, and others, upon all of them be the best of prayers and peace. He saw of Our signs what We had decreed for him, and he returned among you to the nearer mosque in that small part of the night, while you strike the livers of camels for this distance a month going and a month returning.

Then He described it with what requires its exaltation and that it is worthy of being aimed for. He said (Exalted is He): ﴿Whose surroundings We have blessed﴾, meaning, by what We possess of greatness, with waters, trees, its being the abode of prophets, the descent place of angels, the homeland of worship, the source of fruits, provisions and blessings. ﴿Around it﴾, meaning for its sake. So what then is your opinion of it itself? It is more eloquent than "Whose surroundings We have blessed." Then from it to the heavens above, to the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary, to what no human other than him has attained, may Allah bless him and his family and grant him peace, and honor, exalt, glorify and magnify him always and forever.

Perhaps He omitted mention of the Mi'raj (the ascension) from the Qur'an here because their understanding falls short of grasping its proofs, were they to deny it. This is unlike the night journey, for He established its proof against them through what they had witnessed of the signs he described to them, while they were certain he had not seen them before that. So when his truthfulness became clear through what he mentioned of the signs, He then informed of whom Allah willed with the ascension.

Then He mentioned, glorified is He, the purpose of the night journey, in a way that increases the magnification of the mosque. He said: ﴿That We might show him﴾, with his eye and his heart, ﴿some of Our signs﴾, the heavenly and the earthly ones, just as We showed his father, the Friend, peace be upon him, the dominion of the heavens and the earth. The shift from the third person to the first person (al-iltifat) is for the magnification of the signs and the blessings.

al-Bukhari narrates from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was brought, on the night he was taken on the night journey, to Iliya' (Jerusalem) with two vessels, one of wine and one of milk. He looked at them, and took the milk. Jibril, peace be upon him, said: 'Praise be to Allah, who guided you to the natural disposition (al-fitrah). Had you taken the wine, your nation would have gone astray.'"

And from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "When Quraysh denied me, I stood in al-Hijr, and Allah made Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem) manifest to me, and I began to inform them of its signs while I was looking at it."

Since what is relied upon, for the most part, in perceiving the signs is the sense of hearing and sight, and since the full benefit of that is only through knowledge, and since He, glorified is He, had singled out this Prophet (ﷺ) with a perfection of the senses, by which the senses of others are considered as nonexistent, He expressed all of that with His saying (Exalted is He): ﴿Indeed He﴾, meaning this servant whom We singled out for the night journey, ﴿He is﴾, meaning exclusively, ﴿the All-Hearing﴾, meaning with ears and heart, responding to Us and submitting to Our commands, ﴿the All-Seeing﴾, seeing with sight and insight, as evidenced by what he reported of the signs and what he confirmed of the proofs, when he described to them what they asked him about concerning Bayt al-Maqdis and the matter of their caravan and other things, which are well known in the story of the night journey. He was seeing what he described to them, while they could not see it, nor came close to it, nor hoped for it. Those among them who had entered Bayt al-Maqdis said: "As for the description, by Allah, he has been correct. Tell us about our caravan." So he told them about the number of its camels and their conditions, and said: "It will arrive on such-and-such a day, at sunrise, led by a grey-brown camel." So they went out that day toward the pass (al-Thaniyyah), running. One of them said: "This is the sun, by Allah, that has risen." Another said: "And this is the caravan, by Allah, that has come, led by a grey-brown camel, just as Muhammad said." Still they did not believe, and said: "This is nothing but evident magic."

Imam al-Razi said in *al-Lawami'*: The Prophet (ﷺ) saw everything in the kingdom and the dominion with his seeing eye, as direct witness, and was never in doubt about it, so much so that it is narrated that he said: "On the night I was taken up on high, I saw the ant crawling on the face of the earth from the Lote-tree of the Utmost Boundary." This was due to the sharpness of his sight. Sight is of several kinds: the sight of the spirit, the sight of the intellect, from which comes tawhid, the sight of nearness (qurbah), which is singled out for the saints, and it is the light of insight (firasah), the sight of prophethood, and the sight of messengerhood. All of these kinds of sight are gathered for our Messenger (ﷺ), and he has in addition the sight of leading and mastering the messengers, for he is the master of the messengers and their leader. He was informed of the realm and the dominion, as he said: "The earth was folded up for me, its easts and its wests." End of quotation. This last was narrated by Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Tirmidhi, from Thawban, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah (Exalted is He) folded the earth up for me, so I saw its easts and its wests."

He used to see behind him as he saw in front of him, as al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others narrated from the hadith of Anas, may Allah be pleased with him. In many of its chains there is no restriction to prayer, and this is explicit that his sight was not confined to the eye, but Allah (Exalted is He) created sight in all of his limbs, and likewise hearing. For the eye being the locus of that, and likewise the ear, is only by Allah's appointment. Had He placed that in other than them, it would have been as He wills, glorified is He, and there is no obstacle. Darkness did not prevent his sight from penetrating.

In the Musnad of Ahmad, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: "I lost my saddle one night, and I passed by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) while he was fastening something for 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her. He said: 'What is the matter with you, Jabir?' I said: 'I have lost my camel, or it has gone off, on a dark night.' He said to me: 'This is your camel; go and take it.' So I went toward where he had said, and did not find it. I returned to him and said: 'May my father and mother be your ransom, O Messenger of Allah, I did not find it.' He said to me: 'Be patient,' until, when he had finished, he took my hand and set off, until we came to the camel, and he handed it to me, and said: 'This is your camel.'" The hadith continues.

al-Bayhaqi, in *Dala'il al-Nubuwwah*, narrates from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to see at night in darkness as he saw in the day in light." The like of this is narrated from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her.

al-Qadi 'Iyad said in *al-Shifa'*: Baqi ibn Makhlad narrated from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) used to see in darkness as he saw in light." He also traced back from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, "from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: When Allah manifested Himself to Musa, peace be upon him, he could see an ant on the rock on a dark night from a distance of ten farsakh."

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 1 (part 2 of 2)**

He permitted that the particular distinction of our Prophet (ﷺ) in this regard came after the Night Journey (al-Isra'); end of quote. Al-Hafiz Nur al-Din al-Haythami (d. 807 AH) included this hadith of Abu Hurayrah in the *Zawa'id* (additions) to the two lexicons of al-Tabarani, *al-Awsat* and *al-Asghar*. Perhaps this is the reason the verse is followed by the mention of Musa (peace be upon him).

Imam Abu Ja'far ibn al-Zubayr said: When His saying (Exalted is He) had preceded, ﴿Indeed, Abraham was a nation, devoutly obedient to Allah, upright﴾ [al-Nahl: 120], up to His saying, ﴿Then We revealed to you, "Follow the religion of Abraham, upright"﴾ [al-Nahl: 123], and so on, the apparent meaning of that was the preference of Abraham (peace be upon him) over Muhammad (ﷺ), and over all the Prophets, especially with the command to follow him. So it was followed by Surah "al-Isra'," which contains some of the distinctions of our Prophet (ﷺ), and which encompasses what is established in the Sahih (of al-Bukhari and Muslim), what is definitively known, and what is agreed upon, namely that he (ﷺ), who was honored, ennobled, esteemed and exalted, is the master of the descendants of Adam. Thus the surah opens with the story of the Night Journey. It includes, as is recorded in Sahih Muslim and elsewhere, that he led the Prophets (peace be upon them) in prayer, and among them were Abraham, Musa, and others among the Prophets, without exception. This is the narration of Thabit from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him). In the hadith of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that he (ﷺ), who was honored, ennobled, esteemed and exalted forever and ever [p. 296], praised his Lord and said: "All praise is due to Allah, who sent me as a mercy to the worlds and as a messenger to all mankind, a bringer of good news and a warner, who sent down to me the Qur'an, in which is an exposition of all things, who made my nation the best nation brought forth for mankind, who made my nation a moderate (middle) nation, who made my nation the first and the last, who expanded my breast, removed from me my burden, raised high my remembrance, and made me the opener and the seal." Abraham (peace be upon him) said: "With this Muhammad (ﷺ) has been made superior to you."

In the narration of Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) through the route of al-Rabi' ibn Anas, and he mentioned the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha), that "He (Blessed and Exalted) said to him: 'Ask.' He said: 'You took Abraham as a close friend (khalil), You gave him a great kingdom, You spoke to Musa directly, You gave Dawud a great kingdom, You made iron pliable for him, You subjected the mountains to him, You gave Sulayman a great kingdom, You subjected the jinn, the humans, the devils, and the winds to him, and You gave him a kingdom that is not to be given to anyone after him. You taught 'Isa the Torah and the Gospel, You made him heal the blind and the leper, and You protected him and his mother from the accursed Satan, so that Satan had no power over them.'" His Lord (Blessed and Exalted) said to him: "I have taken you as a beloved friend (habib). It is written in the Torah: 'Muhammad is the beloved of the Most Merciful.' I have sent you to mankind as a whole. I have made your nation the first and the last. I have made your nation such that no sermon (khutbah) is valid for them until they testify that you are My servant and My messenger. I have made you the first of the Prophets in creation and the last in resurrection. I have given you seven of the oft-repeated (al-Mathani), which I did not give to any Prophet before you. I have given you the final verses of Surah al-Baqarah from a treasure beneath the Throne, which I did not give to any Prophet before you. And I have made you the opener and the seal."

In the hadith of Shurayk that he saw Musa (peace be upon him) in the seventh heaven. He said: [Musa was preferred] for the speech of Allah. He said: Then he (ﷺ) ascended beyond that to a place that none knows but Allah. Musa then said: "I did not think that anyone would be raised above me."

In the hadith of Ali ibn Abi Talib (may Allah be pleased with him), recorded by al-Bazzar, in the mention of his (peace be upon him) being taught the call to prayer (adhan) and the emergence of the angel, he (ﷺ) said: "O Jibril, who is this?" He said: "By Him who sent you with the truth, I am indeed the closest of creation in station, and this angel I had never seen before since I was created, before this hour of mine." And in it: "Then the angel took the hand of Muhammad (ﷺ) and brought him forward, and he led the people of the heavens in prayer, among whom were Adam and Nuh [p. 298]."

In this hadith Abu Ja'far Muhammad ibn Ali ibn al-Husayn, its narrator, said: "On that day Allah perfected for Muhammad (ﷺ), who was honored, ennobled, esteemed and exalted, the nobility over the people of the heavens and the earth."

Ibn al-Zubayr said: His preference (ﷺ), who was honored, ennobled, esteemed and exalted forever and ever, has been achieved through the Night Journey and his particular distinction in it. Then the surah encompasses the mention of the praiseworthy station (al-Maqam al-Mahmud), which is his station of the Great Intercession (al-Shafa'ah al-Kubra). This is among the things he was specially granted, as established in the Sahih and as agreed upon by the consensus (ijma') of the People of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah). I know of no surah in the Noble Book that includes, of the distinctions of him (ﷺ), who was honored, ennobled, esteemed and exalted forever and ever, by which he surpassed all the Prophets (upon them be the best of prayers and peace), as much as this one includes. And praise be to Allah. End of quote.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 2:

When the reality of this extraordinary sign had established what He had told about His holy self, namely His immense power over everything He wills, and what He had granted to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, of clear signs in this short span of time, He followed it with what was given in the journey from Egypt to the Holy Land of signs, over very long periods, to Musa, peace be upon him, who was the greatest of the prophets in blessing for this community on the night of the Isra' (the Night Journey). This was because of what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, was guided to of returning to Allah (exalted be He) to ask for the lightening of the prayer, until it was reduced from fifty to five, with the reward of fifty. And [Musa was the one] whose ascent was ended with him, when Allah conversed with him and brought him near to the summit of Mount Sinai, after the command to discipline himself through fasting and seclusion for forty days. And what preceded at the end of "al-Nahl" (The Bee), that his people disagreed with him concerning the Sabbath, as a warning against the like of their condition and as consolation regarding those who followed them in their denial and their misguidance. This was in a context warning those who deny of the great calamities. So He said (exalted be He), linking it to what is implied by His saying: "We gave Our servant Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, the Book, the detailed and miraculous, and made it a guidance for all creation, and took upon Ourselves its preservation, so it became an enduring sign, a perpetual guardian of his religion":

﴿And We gave﴾; that is, by Our greatness; ﴿Musa the Book﴾; that is, the one comprehensive of the good of both abodes, for his piety and his goodness, magnifying him by the plural of majesty. Thus He equated the two prophets in the magnification of the showing and the giving. He specified Muhammad, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, by attributing his signs to the locus of majesty. The giving of the Book to Musa, peace be upon him, was in roughly forty-odd years after he brought the Children of Israel out with him from the snares of Pharaoh and his armies, who were countless in number, by those awesome signs, about which no sensible person doubts that whoever has power over them is not prevented from anything he wills. During this long period, (p-300) and even more, the arrival of the Children of Israel from Egypt to this Mosque to which We brought Our servant, and returned him to you, took place in a part of a single night, riding the Buraq, which the prophets before him used to ride, placing its hoof at the farthest reach of its sight. The Children of Israel used to travel all day, striving, then camp at the place from which they had set out, in the wilderness (al-Tih), unable to cross it for forty years, according to what many scholars have said; or they were during this period circling around Mount Edom, as in the Torah. Thus it is established that We act by choice, according to what We see of wisdoms. Then He mentioned the fruit of the Book of Musa, peace be upon him, saying (exalted be He): ﴿And We made it﴾; that is, the Book, by what We have of majesty; ﴿a guidance﴾. Since this tanwin (indefinite marker) could be for magnification, encompassing all guidance, He clarified the condition with His saying: ﴿for the Children of Israel﴾, by directing them to justice in monotheism and the rulings. We made Musa, peace be upon him, and his people journey from Egypt to the lands of the Farthest Mosque, and they stayed traveling toward it for forty years without arriving, and every one of them who had come out of Egypt died except the two chiefs who fulfilled the covenant. Thus the separation between the two journeys became clear, (p-301) just as the separation between the two Books became clear. So the mention of the Night Journey first is evidence for the omission of its like for Musa, peace be upon him, second; and the mention of the giving of the Book second is evidence for the omission of its like first. Therefore the verse belongs to the rhetorical device of ihtibak (balanced omission, in which each part's absence is indicated by the other). Then He alerted that the purpose of all of this is monotheism, in belief and worship, by His saying (exalted be He): ﴿That not﴾; that is, lest; ﴿you take﴾; with the yaa (third person) in the reading of Abu 'Amr, and with the taa (second person) in the reading of the rest. He alerted, by the form of ifti'al (reflexive form), that because of the abundance of proofs of His oneness, and the qualities and virtues He has toward His creation, one does not turn away from Him to other than Him except with great strain upon the self and conflict between desire and reason, and against what He, glorified be He, has instilled in souls of submission to Him and turning toward Him. He repelled from Him, with those of lofty aspiration and noble soul, shirk, by His saying, alerting through the prepositional phrase to the multiplicity of ranks below the rank of His greatness, glorified be He, and their not reaching it; leaving the nun of majesty to make the intended meaning explicit, without ambiguity in any way: ﴿besides Me﴾. And He said (exalted be He): ﴿as a guardian﴾; that is, a lord to whom they entrust their affairs and on whom they rely; from an idol or anything else, to bring them closer to Him by intercession or otherwise. Alerting through the mention of guardianship to the folly of their opinions (p-302) in abandoning the One who suffices for everything in favor of one who has no sufficiency for anything. Then He followed it with what indicates their honor through the honor of their father, and that their reliance on him did not benefit them when He willed retribution, because of the crimes they committed. So He said, alerting to the importance of monotheism and the command to sincerity, returning to the locus of majesty where there is no ambiguity, placing it in the accusative by specification in the reading of Abu 'Amr, and in the vocative according to the rest, as a reminder of the blessing of deliverance from drowning:

﴿The offspring of those whom We carried﴾; that is, in the Ark, by Our greatness, upon the back of that water which covered what lies beneath the vault of the sky. He drew attention to their nobility and the completeness of His favour upon them by His saying (exalted is He): ﴿with Noah﴾; that is, from among his children and their children, the most noble of whom were Abraham, who was grateful, and then Israel, peace be upon them both. This is because the correct view is that those who were with him from among others died and left no descendants. He did not say "the offspring of Noah," so that it would be known that they are the descendants of his believing children, and so that this would be another favour. Then He drew attention to Noah's piety and goodness, as an incitement to follow him, by His saying: ﴿Indeed he was﴾; that is, by a natural disposition, ﴿a grateful servant﴾; that is, one who was exceedingly thankful. Gratitude is the directing of all the blessings that God has bestowed upon a person toward what He created them for. Therefore God was good to him in return for his gratitude, by placing prophethood and the Book in his descendants, as He did with Abraham (peace be upon him), because he was grateful. So follow these two great forefathers in gratitude, and He will increase you, and do not imitate anyone else in disbelief, or He will punish you.

He singled out Noah because God gave no one as much respite as He gave his people, nor granted anyone as much delay as He granted them. Then He destroyed them all, as His saying "We carried" alludes to, with the ease of destroying a single soul. Then He removed the water after drowning them, gradually, over a long period. Thus it is established that He is free of haste, and that He, glory be to Him, sometimes does many arduous things in the briefest time, and sometimes does what is lesser over long periods. It is therefore clear as the sun that He acts according to what He wills, in accordance with what His wisdom requires.

Al-Bukhari (d. 256 AH) related in his Tafsir (the chapter on the exegesis of the Qur'an), from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was brought some meat, and the foreleg was lifted to him, as he liked it. He took a bite from it, then said: 'I am the master of mankind on the Day of Resurrection. Do you know why? Allah will gather the people, the first and the last, on one plain. The caller will make them hear, and the sight will reach them all. The sun will draw near, and the people will suffer distress and anguish beyond their endurance and capacity. The people will say: Do you not see what has befallen you? Will you not look for someone who will intercede for you with your Lord?'" He then mentioned the hadith of the Great Intercession, and their coming to the Prophets: Adam, and after him the Messengers of firm resolve (Ulu l-'Azm), peace be upon them all. They say to Noah (peace be upon him): "Allah has called you a grateful servant." Each of them disclaims it and refers to the one after him, until the matter reaches our Prophet (ﷺ), and they say: "O Muhammad, you are the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets, and Allah has forgiven you what preceded of your sins and what followed. Intercede for us with our Lord. Do you not see what we are in?" "So I set out and come beneath the Throne, and I fall down in prostration to my Lord. Then Allah opens upon me praises of Him and fine commendation of Him, such as He has not opened upon anyone before me. Then it is said: 'O Muhammad, raise your head; ask and you shall be given; intercede and your intercession shall be accepted.' So I raise my head and say: 'My community, O Lord! My community, O Lord!' Then it is said: 'O Muhammad, admit from your community those who will have no reckoning through the right-hand door of the gates of Paradise; and they will share with the people in the other doors.'" Then he said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, the distance between the two leaves of a door of Paradise is like the distance between Makkah and Himyar, or like the distance between Makkah and Busra."

Then He followed that with what indicates the nobility of the Book of Moses and the soundness of its attribution to Him (exalted is He), with what necessitates the comprehensiveness of knowledge and the completeness of power, through what time has revealed of the truthfulness of His reports and the severity of His threat and warning, as a reminder that whoever denies His Book, He destroys him, whoever he may be, even if His respite is prolonged; so do not be deceived by His forbearance, for kings do not tolerate a matter that undermines their kingdom. So He (exalted is He) said: ﴿And We decreed﴾; that is, by Our majesty, through the decisive revelation, [sending down and making known]; ﴿to the Children of Israel﴾; that is, Our servant Ya'qub (peace be upon him), who was the most obedient of the people of his time to Us; ﴿in the Book﴾, which We delivered to them through the tongue of Musa (peace be upon him); ﴿that you will surely cause corruption﴾; He emphasized it by indicating an oath with the lam, because corruption seems unlikely alongside a guiding Book; ﴿in the land﴾; that is, the Holy Land, which, because of its nobility, is as if it were "the land" itself; by that which angers Allah; ﴿twice﴾; ﴿and you will surely become haughty with great haughtiness﴾; that is, through what you came to of insolence, due to forgetting the Benefactor; by wrongdoing and rebellion. And We will not take vengeance upon you except in accordance with what Our wisdom requires, at the time We will, after a long respite. And "al-qada'" (decree): the decisive settling of a matter with firm determination.

[p. 306] Meaning: its time, which We appointed for it, for retribution to take place. ﴿So when the promise of the first of them came﴾. ﴿We sent﴾, meaning with Our might. By His words ﴿against you﴾ He indicated that they were enemies. By His words (exalted is He) ﴿servants of Ours﴾ He indicated His greatness, His power, and the vastness of His dominion, meaning that you have no power against them, because of the might We bestowed upon them. ﴿Possessors of might﴾, meaning of punishment and of severe fierceness in war. ﴿Of great force, so they went through﴾, meaning they roamed, with oppression, harshness, and fierce violence. Al-Jaws (searching through) means seeking something thoroughly. ﴿Between﴾, meaning among. ﴿The dwellings﴾, which entails the subjugation of their people and their humiliation after that great elevation. Al-Khilal (the space between) is the opening between two things, or more, [and it is used] for a kind of weakness. ﴿And it was﴾, meaning that sending and the promise of punishment through it. ﴿A promise to be fulfilled﴾, meaning there is no doubt about its occurrence, and it must be carried out, because there is no barrier between Us and it, and none alters the word except one who is incapable or ignorant.

From Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they were Jalut (Goliath) and his soldiers. From Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib that they were Bukhtnassar (Nebuchadnezzar) and his soldiers. From al-Hasan: the 'Amaliqah (Amalekites). From Sa'id ibn Jubayr: Sanjarib (Sennacherib) and his soldiers. In the Fifth Book of the Torah (indicating this first time, and Allah knows best), he said:

(If you do not hear the word of the LORD your God, and do not keep and do not observe all His statutes which I command you today, all this curse will come upon you and overtake you; you will be cursed in the city and cursed in the field; your nest and the fruit of your land will be cursed; you will be cursed when you come in and cursed when you go out. The LORD will send upon you plague and pestilence and severe blows, and upon everything you put your hand to do, until He destroys you and ruins you quickly, because of the evil of your deeds and your forsaking My worship. The LORD will send upon you death, and it will destroy you from the land you are entering to possess. The LORD will strike you with madness of mind, and with leprosy, and with the burning by the fire, and with jaundice, and with scab, and with the poison; and He will bring these peoples upon you until you perish; and the heaven above you will be bronze and the earth beneath you iron; the LORD will turn the rain of your land into dust; and the LORD will defeat you before your enemies; you will go out against them by one way and flee by seven ways; and you will become a horror and a fear to all the kingdoms of the earth; and your corpses will be food for all the beasts and birds of the sky, and no one will drive them away; and the LORD will strike you with the sores with which He struck the people of Egypt, and He will afflict you with leprosy, dysentery, and itch, and there will be no cure for you; the LORD will strike you with blindness, and with confusion, and with terror of heart; you will grope at noon as the blind grope; nothing you do will prosper; you will be oppressed, robbed, and violated all the days of your life; and there will be no one to save you; you will betroth a woman and another will marry her; you will build a house and another will dwell in it; you will plant vineyards and not harvest from them; you will slaughter your oxen before your eyes and not eat from them; your donkey will be taken from you by force and you will not be able to recover it; your sheep will be driven off by the enemy and there will be no one to save you; your sons and daughters will be taken captive by another people, and you will look on, and be unable to help them; you will be wretched, and you will grieve all day long, and you will have no recourse; the produce of your land and all your toil will be eaten by a people you do not know; and you will be oppressed and wronged all your life;)

[p. 307–308] Then he said: (The LORD will also bring upon you a people, who will come against you while you are hungry and thirsty; and you will serve your enemies whom the LORD will send against you, from afar, from the end of the earth; a nation will swoop down on you like an eagle, a nation whose language you do not understand; a fierce-faced nation which will not respect the old or pity the young; and they will besiege you in all your towns until your high and fortified walls, in which you trust, fall; and you will be reduced, in the hunger and distress which your enemy inflicts upon you, to eating the flesh of your own children; the man who is delicate and refined among you, his eye will be evil toward his brother and his beloved wife and the remnant of his children, so that he will not give to any of them the flesh of his children that he eats, because nothing will be left to him in the siege and distress with which your enemy will oppress you in all your towns; and the woman who is tender and delicate among you, who would not venture to set the sole of her foot on the ground because of her delicacy, her eye will be evil toward her husband, her son and her daughter, and toward her child that she bears, and she will eat them, because of the hunger, the want, and the lack of food, with which your enemy will distress you and oppress you in all your towns.)

[p. 308–309] Then he said: (The LORD will strike you with an evil sore on your knees and your legs, which cannot be healed; and He will bring the wounds upon you from the crown of your head to the sole of your foot; the LORD will drive you and your king whom you have set over you to a nation which you and your fathers have not known; and there you will serve gods of wood and stone; and you will become a sign and a wonder, and everyone who hears of you will be astonished at you;) then he said: (Sons and daughters will be born to you, but they will not remain yours, for they will be taken captive, and led away as captives.)

Then he said: (The LORD will set over you a nation that comes against you while you are hungry and thirsty, and you will serve your enemies whom God sends against you, from afar, from the ends of the earth; a nation swoops down on you like an eagle flies, a nation whose language you do not understand; a nation with fierce faces, which shows no respect for the aged and no mercy to the young; it will besiege you in all your towns until your high and fortified walls fall, in which you trusted; and you will be driven, by the hunger and distress which your enemy inflicts upon you, to eat the flesh of your own children...)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 6 (part 1 of 4):

When He, glorified is He, had shown that He is able to humble the mighty after the greatness of their power, He showed that He is capable of granting them victory over those who overcame them after their long humiliation, once He had cleansed them of their filth and purified them of their sins. So He, exalted is He, said, indicating by the particle of delay (*thumma*) the magnitude of this restoration, since it breaks with customary patterns: ﴿Then We gave back to you the return (of power)﴾; that is, by what We possess of greatness. He hastened to give them good news by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿to you﴾, that is, specifically; ﴿the return﴾, that is, the recovery and the greatness. He showed that this was accompanied by might by His saying, glorified is He: ﴿over them﴾. Some of the exegetes said: this was in the time of Dawud (David), peace be upon him. ﴿And We aided you﴾, that is, We helped you ﴿with wealth﴾, which you use to fight your enemies; ﴿and sons﴾, that is, by whom you are strengthened; ﴿and We made you﴾, that is, by Our greatness, ﴿more numerous﴾, that is, than your enemy, ﴿in manpower﴾, that is, people who would go forth with you when you called them out to fight and to other urgent matters.

(p-311) It is evident that this second time does not refer to what happened at the hands of Dawud, peace be upon him, because God says, in this second time: ﴿and that they might enter the Sanctuary as they entered it the first time﴾ [al-Isra': 7]. Dawud, peace be upon him, founded the Sanctuary but did not complete it; rather, his son Sulayman, peace be upon them both, completed it after him. What deceived those who said this is that the Children of Israel had been overcome before Dawud, peace be upon him, by the Philistines and others, and then their deliverance came at his hands, peace be upon him, as the allusion to it has already passed in surah al-Baqarah. He said in the *Zabur* (the Psalms), in Psalm thirteen: "Who will give Zion salvation for Israel? When the LORD restores the captivity of His people, Jacob will rejoice and Israel will be glad." And in Psalm forty-three:

(p-312) "O God, we have heard with our ears, and our fathers have told us the works that You did in their days, in the times of old. So we will praise You, O our God, every day, and give thanks to Your name forever. Yet now You have cast us off and humbled us, and You, O LORD, did not go out with our armies. But You made us turn back from our enemies, and those who hate us have plundered us for themselves. You have given us like sheep to be eaten, and have scattered us among the nations. You sold Your people for nothing, and did not profit by their price. You have made us a reproach to our neighbors, a scorn and a derision to those around us. You have made us a byword among the nations, a shaking of the head among the peoples. All day long my dishonor is before me, and shame has covered my face, because of the voice of him who reproaches and blasphemes. O God, all this has come upon us, yet we have not forgotten You, nor have we dealt falsely with Your covenant. Our heart has not turned back, nor have our steps departed from Your way, though You have crushed us in a place of jackals and covered us with the shadow of death. If we had forgotten the name of our God, or stretched out our hands to a foreign god, would not God search this out? For He knows the secrets of the heart. Awake! Why do You sleep, O LORD? Arise, do not cast us off forever. Why do You hide Your face and forget our affliction and our oppression?" And in Psalm seventy-eight and the one after it:

(p-313) "O God, the nations have come into Your inheritance; they have defiled Your holy temple; they have laid Jerusalem in heaps. They have given the dead bodies of Your servants as food to the birds of the heavens, the flesh of Your saints to the beasts of the earth. They have poured out their blood like water all around Jerusalem, and there was no one to bury them. We have become a reproach to our neighbors, a scorn and derision to those around us. How long, O LORD? Will You be angry forever? Will Your jealousy burn like fire? Pour out Your wrath on the nations that do not know You, and on the kingdoms that do not call on Your name. For they have devoured Jacob and laid waste his habitation. Do not remember against us our former iniquities; let Your compassion come quickly to meet us, for we are brought very low. Help us, O God of our salvation, for the glory of Your name; deliver us and forgive our sins for Your name's sake. Why should the nations say, 'Where is their God?' Let the avenging of the blood of Your servants which has been shed be known among the nations before our eyes. Let the groaning of the prisoners come before You; according to the greatness of Your power preserve those who are doomed to die. Repay our neighbors sevenfold into their bosom the reproach with which they have reproached You, O Lord! We are Your people and the sheep of Your pasture; we will give You thanks forever; from generation to generation we will declare Your praise." "Give ear, O Shepherd of Israel, You who lead Joseph like a flock; You who are enthroned between the cherubim, shine forth! Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh, stir up Your might, and come to save us! Restore us, O God; cause Your face to shine, that we may be saved. O LORD God of hosts, how long will You be angry with the prayer of Your people? You have fed them with the bread of tears, and given them tears to drink in large measure. You have made us a source of contention to our neighbors, and our enemies laugh among themselves. Restore us, O God of hosts; cause Your face to shine, that we may be saved. You brought a vine out of Egypt; You drove out the nations and planted it. You prepared room for it, and it took deep root and filled the land. The mountains were covered with its shadow, and the mighty cedars with its branches. It sent out its boughs to the sea, and its shoots to the River. Why have You broken down its walls, so that all who pass by pluck its grapes? The boar from the forest ravages it, and the wild beasts devour it. Return, we beseech You, O God of hosts; look down from heaven, and see; visit this vine and the stock which Your right hand has planted, and the son whom You made strong for Yourself. It is burned with fire; it is cut down; they perish at the rebuke of Your countenance. Let Your hand be upon the man of Your right hand, upon the son of man whom You made strong for Yourself. Then we will not turn away from You; revive us, and we will call upon Your name. Restore us, O LORD God of hosts; cause Your face to shine, that we may be saved."

And in Psalm eighty-four: "LORD, You were favorable to Your land; You restored the fortunes of Jacob. You forgave the iniquity of Your people; You covered all their sin. You took away all Your wrath; You turned from the fierceness of Your anger." And in Psalm eighty-eight: "Holy One of Israel, our King by revelation, You spoke to Your prophet and said: 'I have given help to one who is mighty; I have exalted one chosen from among the people. I have found David My servant; with My holy oil I have anointed him. My hand shall be established with him; My arm also shall strengthen him. The enemy shall not outwit him, nor the son of wickedness afflict him. I will beat down his foes before his face and strike those who hate him. My faithfulness and My mercy shall be with him, and in My name his horn shall be exalted. I will set his hand also over the sea and his right hand over the rivers. He shall cry to Me, "You are my Father, my God, and the rock of my salvation." Also I will make him My firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth. My mercy I will keep for him forever, and My covenant shall stand firm with him.'" Then he said: "But You have cast off and rejected Your anointed; You have been full of wrath against him. You have renounced the covenant of Your servant; You have defiled his crown by casting it to the ground. You have broken down all his walls; You have brought his strongholds to ruin. All who pass by plunder him; he has become a reproach to his neighbors. You have exalted the right hand of his adversaries; You have made all his enemies rejoice. You have also turned back the edge of his sword, and You have not supported him in battle. You have made his splendor to cease, and cast his throne down to the ground. The days of his youth You have shortened; You have covered him with shame. How long, O LORD? Will You hide Yourself forever? Will Your wrath burn like fire? Remember how short my time is; for what futility You have created all the sons of men! What man can live and not see death? Can he deliver his soul from the power of the grave? O Lord, where are Your former lovingkindnesses, which You swore to David in Your truth? Remember, O Lord, the reproach of Your servants, how I bear in my bosom the reproach of all the mighty peoples, with which Your enemies have reproached, O LORD, with which they have reproached the footsteps of Your anointed. Blessed be the LORD forever! Amen and Amen." And in Psalm one hundred and five: "Save us, O LORD our God, and gather us from among the nations, to give thanks to Your holy name and to triumph in Your praise. Blessed be the LORD God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting! And let all the people say, 'Amen! Praise the LORD!'" And in Psalm one hundred and twenty-five: "When the LORD brought back the captivity of Zion, we were like those who dream. Then our mouth was filled with laughter, and our tongue with singing. Then they said among the nations, 'The LORD has done great things for them.' The LORD has done great things for us, and we are glad. Bring back our captivity, O LORD, as the streams in the South. Those who sow in tears shall reap in joy. He who continually goes forth weeping, bearing seed for sowing, shall indeed come again with joy, bringing his sheaves with him." And in Psalm one hundred and thirty-six: "By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat down, yes, we wept when we remembered Zion. We hung our harps upon the willows in the midst of it. For there those who carried us away captive asked of us a song, and those who plundered us requested mirth, saying, 'Sing us one of the songs of Zion!' How shall we sing the LORD's song in a foreign land? If I forget you, O Jerusalem, let my right hand forget its skill! If I do not remember you, let my tongue cling to the roof of my mouth; if I do not exalt Jerusalem above my chief joy. Remember, O LORD, against the children of Edom the day of Jerusalem, who said, 'Raze it, raze it, down to its foundation!' O daughter of Babylon, you who are to be destroyed, happy shall he be who repays you as you have served us! Happy shall he be who takes your little ones and dashes them against the rock!"

(p-318) What is in this psalm is an announcement of what will befall them from Bukhtnasar (Nebuchadnezzar). It has been mentioned more than once that whatever is transmitted from these ancient books containing a word that suggests deficiency, such as "the Father" and the like, then even if it is correctly attributed to them, it is not permissible to apply it in our law. It is evident that these proofs mentioned in the Qur'an in this return were those that took place in the days of 'Uzayr (Ezra), peace be upon him, at the hand of Kurash (Cyrus), king of the Persians, as will come, God willing, the Exalted. And those who had overcome them first were the armies of Bukhtnasar, as has already been mentioned. In the Book of the Prophets of the Children of Israel, who came after Musa (Moses), peace be upon him, it is recorded that God, exalted is He, revealed to Iramya ibn Hilqiya (Jeremiah), (p-319) one of the rabbis who were in 'Anathoth in the land of Binyamin (Benjamin), in the reign of Yushiya (Josiah), king of Yuhdha (Judah), in the thirteenth year of his reign, warning them that if they did not turn back from the errors they had introduced, He would give power over them to the king of Babylon. He did not cease warning them of the same, and informing them of the evil that would come upon them because of their sins, until the days of Yawakim (Jehoiakim), son of Yushiya, and in the eleventh year of Sidqiya (Zedekiah), son of Yushiya, until the day Jerusalem was taken captive in the fifth month, which is the month of Ab. He used to inform them that the king of Babylon would capture Sidqiya, king of the Jews, and lead him with the captives to Babylon, and that they would remain in captivity for seventy years. Then God, exalted is He, would return them to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem).

[p. 320] Jeremiah (peace be upon him) said: "God (Exalted) said to me: (Before I formed you in the womb I knew you, and before you came out of the womb I set you apart for Myself as a prophet; and I made you a prophet to the peoples). I said: I beseech You, O Lord, my God, to excuse me, for I do not know how to speak, because I am a youth. The Lord said to me: (Do not say, 'I am a youth,' for you will go to everything to which I send you, and you will speak whatever I command you. So deliver it, and do not fear, for I am with you; I will rescue you from every calamity). The Lord stretched out His hand and brought it near my mouth, and the Lord said to me: (I have put My words in your mouth. Know that I have set you this day over all the kingdoms of the nations, to tear down, to break down, to destroy, to uproot, to rebuke, to prophesy, and to sanctify Me). Then the Lord revealed to me and said: (What do you see, Jeremiah?). I said: I see a branch of an almond tree. The Lord said to me: (You have seen well, for I am hastening My word to fulfillment). Then the Lord revealed to me a second time: (What do you see?). I said: a boiling pot, its face turned toward the north (al-Jirbiyya, i.e., the north). The Lord said to me: (From the north the evil will break open and come down upon all the land of Judah. Behold, I am sending you to call all the families of the kingdoms of the north). The Lord says: (They will come, and each man will set his throne at the entrance of the gates of Jerusalem, and they will surround its walls, and all the cities of Judah. I will judge them with My judgments and My decrees, because of all their wickedness, for they have forsaken Me, burned incense to other gods, and bowed down to the work of their hands. But as for you, gird up your loins, arise, and speak to them all the words that I command you. Do not be afraid of them, and do not favor them, lest I break you before them and humble you. I have made you this day like a fortified city, like an iron pillar, and like a bronze wall against the whole land, against the kings of Judah, its princes, its priests, its fathers, and all the people of the land. They will fight against you, but they will not prevail over you, for I am with you, and I will deliver you from them)".

He continued to stand among them speaking words of this kind, of the utmost eloquence and tenderness, so that they would crush hearts, split the breast, and cause the eyes to overflow, for about four quires. Had it not been for fear of tedium and dislike of prolixity, I would have quoted much of it. The false prophets used to stand among them saying the opposite, things that gave them security, until [p. 322] they struck Jeremiah so that he would cease such speech; but he could not stop. He said to a man among the false prophets named Hananiah: The Lord has not sent you; you have caused this people to trust in falsehood. Therefore the Lord says: Behold, I will remove you from the face of the earth, and in this year you will die, because you have spoken rebellion against the Lord. Hananiah the false prophet died that year, in the seventh month. Then Jeremiah's warning to them increased, until they imprisoned him. Then God (Exalted) commanded him to write for them what He revealed to him on a scroll and send it to them. So he summoned Baruch son of Neriah, the scribe, and commanded him to write what the Lord had caused him to speak. He said to him: Behold, I am imprisoned, and I cannot enter the house of the Lord. So take this scroll and go into the house of the Lord on the day of fasting and read it to them, for it is the word of the Lord, that perhaps they will turn back from their evil way, and the Lord will relent from the evil He has spoken against them, for great is the wrath and fury with which the Lord has spoken against this people. Baruch did so. They took the scroll from his hand and brought it to King Yawaqim son of Yusiyya, [p. 323] and he tore it and burned it with fire. Then God commanded him to write another scroll like it, adding what God commanded him. Among its contents: Yawaqim, king of Judah, shall have no one to sit on the throne of David (peace be upon him); his corpse shall be cast out to the heat by day and to the frost by night. I will bring upon him, his offspring, and his servants, and upon Jerusalem, its inhabitants, and the house of Judah, all the evil that I have spoken against them, because they did not listen to My voice.

When Sidqiyya ruled over the Jews, in the tenth year of his reign, which was the eighteenth year of Bukhtansar, king of Babylon, the armies of the king of Babylon surrounded Jerusalem. Jeremiah the prophet was imprisoned in the guardhouse of the king, where Sidqiyya, king of Judah, had confined him, and said to him: Why do you prophesy and say: Thus says the Lord: Behold, I will deliver this city and Sidqiyya, king of Judah, into the hands of the king of Babylon, and he will take it, and no one will escape from the hands of the Chaldeans, for the Lord is the deliverer; He will give him into the hand of the king of Babylon, [p. 324] and his mouth will speak to his mouth, his eyes to his eyes, and he will take him to Babylon? God revealed to Jeremiah, while he was imprisoned, and he said: The Lord says: Behold, I will deliver this city to the king of Babylon, and he will burn it with fire. As for you, you will not escape from his hands; rather you will certainly be seized and delivered to him; your eyes will look into his eyes, your mouth will speak with his mouth, and you will go to Babylon. But hear the word of the Lord, O Sidqiyya, king of Judah: Thus says the Lord concerning you: You will not die by the sword, but you will die in peace, and as they mourned over your fathers, the former kings who were before you, so they will mourn over you, saying: Alas, my lord! For this word that I have spoken is the word of the Lord. All of this, and the armies of the king of Babylon are besieging Jerusalem and fighting against it.

Then Sidqiyya sent to Pharaoh in Egypt seeking help from him, and his army went out. When the Chaldeans heard of them, they withdrew from Jerusalem. The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah, that thus says the Lord, the God of Israel, to the king of Judah who sent to the army of Pharaoh to help him: Behold, the army of Pharaoh is now returning to the land of Egypt, and the Chaldeans will return, [p. 325] fight against this city, capture it, and burn it with fire. Thus says the Lord: Do not think in your souls that the Chaldeans who have withdrawn from you will not return; rather they will return and burn the city with fire. Then the Jews accused Jeremiah of wanting to flee to the Chaldeans, so they beat him and cast him into prison. King Sidqiyya brought him out and secretly asked him in the house about the word of the Lord. He said to him: You will be given into the hand of the king of Babylon. And he said to him: What wrong have I done to you, to your servants, or to this people, that you have cast me into prison? Where are those who prophesied to you that the king of Babylon would not come upon you or upon this land? He returned him to prison, and did not put him into the pit, because he could not oppose the nobles of his kingdom.

Then Jeremiah said: Thus says the Lord: Whoever remains in this city will die by the sword, by famine, and by pestilence; but whoever goes out to the Chaldeans will save his life and live. Thus says the Lord. [p. 326] The nobles said: This man must be put to death, for he weakens the hands of the warriors who remain in the city and the hands of the people when he speaks these words. King Sidqiyya said: Behold, he is in your hands; the king can do nothing against you. The king was not able to say anything to them. So they took Jeremiah and cast him into the pit of Malkiah son of the king, in the prison court. The pit had no water, but mire, and Jeremiah sank into the mire. A Cushite servant of the king, who was a believing man, heard, and he said to the king: My lord, evil is what these people have done to the prophet, casting him into a pit, and behold, he is dying. The king said: Take with you thirty men from here and go up and bring Jeremiah up from the pit before he dies. The king's servant took men and entered the storehouse beneath the king's house, took from there some worn rags, and lowered them to Jeremiah with a rope, and said to him: Take these rags and put them under your armpits, lest the rope hurt you. Jeremiah did so, and they drew him up from the pit and seated him in the prison court. [p. 327] The king sent for Jeremiah and had him brought to him, and placed him within three chambers, one inside another. He said to him: I ask you not to hide anything from me. Jeremiah said to Sidqiyya: I fear that you will kill me, and if I advise you, you will not obey me. Sidqiyya said: As the Lord lives, who created me, I will not kill you, nor will I give you to the people who seek your life. Jeremiah said: Thus says the Lord, the God of Israel: If you go out to the princes of the king of Babylon, you will save your life, and this city will be spared and not burned with fire, and you and your sons will live. But if you do not go out to them, this city will be given to the Chaldeans, and they will burn it with fire, and you will not escape from their hands. The king said to Jeremiah: I fear the Jews, that I may go out to the Chaldeans, lest they hand me over to them and mock me. Jeremiah said: They will not hand you over to them; listen to the word of the Lord for your own benefit, that you may save your life.

The word of the Lord came to Jeremiah while he was imprisoned in the guardhouse: Go and say to the Cushite servant of the king: Thus says the Lord, the Mighty One, the God of [p. 328] Israel: Behold, I will bring evil upon this city, and they will be before you on that day, and I will save you. The Lord said: You will not be given into the hand of the people who do not fear God, nor will you fall in battle, but you will save yourself, because you have trusted in what the Lord has said to you.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 6 (part 3 of 4):

Irmiya remained in the house of the prison until the day on which the Chaldeans (al-Kaldaniyyun) took Urshalim (Jerusalem), in the ninth year of Sidqiya, king of Yahuda (Judah), in the tenth month, on the ninth day of the month. Bukhtansar (Nebuchadnezzar), king of Babil (Babylon), came with all his troops to Urshalim and besieged it. In the eleventh year of Sidqiya, in the fifth month, the city was breached. All the nobles of the king of Babil came and sat at the middle gate. When Sidqiya saw that they had sat at the middle gate, and that the fighting men had fled and gone out by night, the king also went out through the gate between the two walls, on the road of Nisan. When he reached the desert, the soldiers of the Chaldeans pursued him on his trail and caught up with him in the desert of Ariha (Jericho), and his troops deserted him. They led him away until they brought him up to Bukhtansar, king of Babil, at Diylab, in the land of Hamat. The king of Babil slaughtered the sons of Sidqiya and all the nobles of Yahuda. He blinded the eyes of Sidqiya, bound him in chains to take him to Babil. The house of the king and the houses of the people were burned with fire, and he tore down the wall that surrounded Urshalim. As for the remnant of the people who remained in the city, and those who had fled to him, he took them captive and handed them over to Wazirdan, the chief of his police, who took them to Babil. As for the poor of the people, who had nothing, he left them in the land of Yahuda and appointed over them Akhiqam ibn Shafan. Bukhtansar commanded the chief of his police to take Irmiya and said: "Let your eye be upon him, do him no harm, and do whatever he tells you." So he sent for Irmiya and took him from the house of confinement, and handed him over to Ajdaliya ibn Akhiqam ibn Shafan, to return him to his house. Wazirdan, the chief of police, said to Irmiya: "Your God who spoke this evil against this town has done just as He said, because you sinned against the Lord and did not listen to His voice, so this matter has come upon you. As for you, behold, I have released you from the chains that were on your hands. If you wish to come with me to Babil, then come; and if you wish, remain. This whole land is before you; go wherever is good and pleasing in your eyes. Otherwise, sit with Ajdaliya ibn Akhiqam ibn Shafan, whom Bukhtansar appointed over Yahuda." The chief of police gave him gifts for the road and sent him away in peace. Irmiya came to Ajdaliya ibn Akhiqam at Mispa and sat with him among the people whom the king of Babil had left in the land.

This is what indicates the people of great might whom God gave power over them. As for what indicates God's mercy toward them: in the history of Yusuf ibn Kariyun, it is recorded that when the Romans learned that Bukhtansar, king of Babil, had conquered the city of al-Maqdis, their fear of the Kasdaniyyin increased. So they sent envoys and gifts to Bukhtansar and asked him for safety and peace. He granted them security and bound them to obedience and allegiance to him, so they were reassured and felt safe, and those wars ceased for them until the time of King Dara. The cause of the wars between the Romans and the Kasdaniyyin was that the Kasdaniyyin were hostile to the Yunaniyyin (Greeks), and the Romans aided the Yunaniyyin, so the Kasdaniyyin became angry at this and fought the people of Rumiya, and the wars between them continued to this extent. When God the Mighty decided to punish the Kasdaniyyin for their long tyranny, and ruled for the end of their kingdom and the termination of their rule, as the prophets had foretold, peace be upon them, He stirred up against them two great kings from among the nations: one was Dara, king of Madai, and the other was Kurush, king of the Persians. Kurush, king of the Persians, married the daughter of Dara, and the two agreed to rebel against the Kasdaniyyin, and he showed opposition to Baltashar ibn Bukhtansar, their king. Then he marched toward Babil with powerful armies. Baltashar sent a large force against them, and a great battle took place between them, in which many were killed on both sides. Then the army of Baltashar was defeated and fled, and Kurush and Dara pursued them for a day's journey from Babil, killing many of them. Dara and Kurush remained at that place. Then Baltashar sent against them a thousand commanders from among his leaders, along with all his close companions and his strongmen. They left Babil at the end of the day and marched through the night, and reached the army of Dara and Kurush at dawn, and attacked them, inflicting a great slaughter. Dara was defeated, but Kurush held firm and fought the Kasdaniyyin, and prevented them from pursuing the army of Dara. The battle continued between them all day. Then the Kasdaniyyin gained the upper hand over the Persians and killed a group of them, and the Persians were defeated. Baltashar's commanders returned to him victorious and laden with spoils, so Baltashar's joy at this greatly increased. He prepared a great feast for his commanders, made it splendid, brought out fine vessels of silver and gold, and went to great lengths to honor them. He attended the drinking gathering with them, and they ate and drank, and their joy and his joy grew. When the wine had taken effect on him, he wanted to increase the honor and happiness of his companions, so he ordered the vessels of gold and silver to be brought, which his grandfather Bukhtansar, the king, had taken from the Temple of Bayt al-Maqdis and carried with the captives of the Children of Israel to Babil. Those vessels were brought in Baltashar's presence, and he drank wine from them, and gave his commanders, his wives, and his concubines to drink from them, and they began to glorify their idols and praise them. He said: So God, Glorified is He, was angered by this, and disliked what Baltashar did in profaning the vessels of holiness, and he did not fear God, nor did he thank Him for granting him victory over his enemies. So He sent an angel and commanded him to write, in Baltashar's presence, words in red, containing mention of what God had decreed against him and against his kingdom. The angel descended by the command of God, Mighty and Majestic, and wrote the words on the wall of the assembly hall opposite the lamp-stand. He could see the fingers of the angel as they wrote, but did not see the rest of his form. Those fingers were extremely bright and luminous. When he saw them, he was stunned, great terror and alarm seized him, and his whole body trembled violently, and all his soldiers were struck with fear. They could not understand that writing, nor did any of his companions find anyone who could read it, because the script was Kasdani and the language was Ibrani.

So he ordered that Daniyal the Prophet, may God's blessings and peace be upon our Prophet Muhammad and upon him, be brought. He read it and interpreted it and said: "O king, you have committed a great error by profaning the vessels of God's holiness through the hands of your soldiers and your concubines, so they defiled them. For this reason God was angered and sent His angel to write these words, to inform you of what He intends to do. As for these written words, they are: (ḥasaba, wazana, naqala). Their interpretation is that God has reckoned the period of your rule, which He had granted you, and found it has come to an end and finished, and nothing of it remains. He weighed you in the balance and found you deficient; that is, He tested you through kindness to you and victory over your enemies, and found you not grateful for His kindness, and you did not praise Him, but instead glorified idols. As for the interpretation of (naqala): God has decreed and ruled that the kingdom be removed from you and transferred to Kurush and Dara." He said: When Baltashar heard what Daniyal had said, his fear and alarm increased, and his commanders were also disturbed and terrified greatly, and they returned to their homes fearful. That night, when Baltashar was asleep, one of his servants came to him and killed him on his bed. He took his head and went to Dara and Kurush and informed them of Baltashar's news, and of what he had done in profaning the vessels of holiness, and of the writing that the angel had written before him, and Daniyal's interpretation of it, and of what Daniyal had told him about the end of his kingdom and the transfer of his rule to the kings of Madai and Fars because of his profaning the vessels of holiness. When Dara and Kurush heard what he had told them and saw Baltashar's head, they thanked God, Mighty and Majestic, acknowledged His power, and greatly glorified and exalted Him. Kurush vowed that he would build the House of God in Urshalim, return those vessels, and release the Jewish captives so that they might return to their lands. Then Kurush and Dara set out from their places, entered Babil, and killed all its inhabitants with the most severe killing and the greatest torment. Thus what the prophets, peace be upon them, had foretold came to pass: God's (Exalted) vengeance upon the Kasdaniyyin and the people of Babil, and their requital for what they had done to the vessels of His holiness. Then Dara and Kurush divided the kingdom of the Kasdaniyyin. Dara took the city of Babil and its territories, and took possession of Baltashar's palace and sat on his throne. Kurush took the whole kingdom of the Kasdaniyyin other than Babil and its territories. The matter was settled between them on this basis. At that time Dara was an old man, so his reign did not last long. When he died, the leaders of Madai and Fars agreed to make Kurush king over them, and from that time the king of Madai and Fars became one. The matter remained so and did not change. When Kurush took possession of the kingdom of the Kasdaniyyin, sat on the throne of Babil, and was made king over Madai and Fars, God (Exalted) stirred him in the first year of his reign, so he recalled his vow that he would release the captives of the Children of Israel to return to their land, and that he would build God's sanctuary and return its vessels to Him. He ordered the elders and chiefs of the captives to be brought, informed them of his resolve to build Bayt al-Maqdis and release them, and said to them: "Whoever among the Jewish captives chooses to go to the city of al-Quds to build the Temple that Bukhtansar destroyed, let him go, and seek help from God, Mighty and Majestic, for He will help him. As for me, Kurush, servant of the Mighty God, I release from my treasuries all the money and equipment he needs for the rebuilding of the House of the Lord, which granted me victory over the Kasdaniyyin and gave me their kingdom." He said: When the elders of the captives heard Kurush's words, their joy greatly increased, and they thanked God, Mighty and Majestic, for His kindness, and they set out for the city of Bayt al-Maqdis, with a large group accompanying them. With them were Ezra the priest, peace be upon him, Nehemiah, Mordecai, Joshua, and the rest of the captives' leaders and chiefs. They built God's House according to the measure Kurush had prescribed for them, built the altar according to its proper size and boundaries, and offered sacrifices in their proper manner. Kurush used to release for them each year whatever they needed for the service of God's House: money, wheat, oil, wine, sheep, and cattle. He released a great deal of money for them, and this practice continued throughout the rule of the Persians. He said: Then Kurush's affairs grew great, and God extended His hand over all the nations and kingdoms, opened for him the strong fortresses, and gave him the treasures and stores of the earth, and he continued to advance and triumph wherever he turned, as God (Exalted) had told through the prophet Ashya, peace be upon him, that He would do this for Kurush, because of his kindness to the Children of Israel.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 6 (part 4 of 4):

He said, in the Book of the Prophets, in the prophecy of Isaiah son of Amoz: (Thus says the LORD: I am He who annuls the signs of the diviners, and turns the knowledge of the soothsayers into folly; I turn back the wise to their rear, and make their counsel foolish; I confirm the word of My servants, and fulfil the counsel of My messengers; who says of Jerusalem, "She shall be inhabited," and of the cities of Judah, "They shall be built, and I will raise up their ruins"; who says to the deep, "Be dry, and I will dry up your rivers"; who says of Cyrus, "He is My shepherd, and shall perform all My pleasure, even saying to Jerusalem, 'You shall be built,' and to the temple, 'Your foundation shall be laid.'" Thus says the LORD to His anointed, to Cyrus, whose right hand I have held, to subdue nations before him and loose the armour of kings, to open doors before him so that gates shall not be shut: "I will go before you and make the crooked places straight; I will break in pieces the doors of bronze and cut through the bars of iron; I will give you the treasures of darkness and hidden riches of secret places, that you may know that I, the LORD, the God of Israel, who call you by your name, am the one. For the sake of My servant Jacob and Israel My chosen, I have called you by your name; I have named you though you did not know Me. I am the LORD, and there is no other God besides Me.") End of what is in the Book of the Prophets.

Cyrus continued to treat the Children of Israel well until he died. His son Tamkisha (Cambyses) reigned after him and carried out what his father had done of righteousness toward the Jews, releasing great wealth to them, glorifying the House of God. The kings of Persia after him continued in this, releasing what Cyrus had released for offerings and other things, honouring the House of God, venerating it, and seeking blessing through it. Then came Ahasuerus, who is Artaxerxes the king, and the condition of the Jews changed in his time, because of a vizier he appointed from the Amalekites, called Haman. Then God (exalted be He) turned him toward them because of a wife he had from the Jews. The affairs of the Jews remained upright while they were under Persian obedience, until Alexander the Second reigned. Ibn Kathir said, in the commentary on Surah al-Kahf: "He is the one from whom the Roman kingdom is dated, and he was about three hundred years before the Messiah." End of quotation. He is the Macedonian, Greek, Roman. He reigned after the killing of his father Philip, and he was twenty years old when he reigned. He was wise, knowledgeable in all the sciences, and the one who taught him wisdom was Aristotle the sage. Alexander used to consult him in his affairs, return to his opinion, and plan by his counsel. He did not resemble his father or his mother. His face was like a lion's face, and his eyes were of different colours: the right black, looking downward, and the left clear in colour, like the eye of a cat, looking upward. His teeth were fine and sharp, like a dog's teeth. He was brave, bold and daring from his youth. When he conquered the lands of the West and returned from them, he headed for the lands of Syria and turned toward Jerusalem. The Angel of the LORD met him and commanded him to honour the Holy City and its people, and he did so. Then he set out for Darius II, king of Persia. When he passed Nablus, Sanballat the Samaritan, its lord, went out to him and brought him great wealth and gifts. Then he marched to Darius and killed him, then to the king of India and did likewise, then to the rising of the sun. Then he desired to see the ends of the earth, so he travelled through them, and saw of the nations and wonders what is mentioned in his biographies. He returned and died at Babylon. Then the affair of the Jews was alternately this and that, while they were under the rule of the Greeks, who reigned after Alexander. Then the Romans prevailed, and the Jews were under their hands. They rose and fell alternately, until calamities multiplied among them, great misfortunes and strife grew, corruption spread, and the Kharijites multiplied among them; killing, treachery, plunder and raids continued. They killed Zechariah and his son Yahya, peace be upon them both, and they agreed to kill the Messiah, son of Mary, peace be upon them both, but God (exalted be He) raised him to Himself. Then He set over them Titus, Caesar, who destroyed them and laid waste the second Temple, as will come. Then no affair has stood for the Jews until now.

When it was established, through the fulfilment of what He threatened at its appointed times as He had told, that His might and His forbearance are real, and so His power and His knowledge are established, He pointed out that the cause of humbling those whom He wishes well is disobedience, and the cause of exalting them is obedience. So He said (Exalted is He): ﴿If you do good﴾; that is, by performing obedience in accordance with the command in the Book that calls to justice and excellence; ﴿you do good to yourselves﴾. For that necessitates My being with you, so I will bring you honour in this world, or in the Hereafter, or in both. ﴿And if you do evil﴾; that is, by committing what is forbidden and by corruption; ﴿then it is for them﴾, the evil. He mentioned it with the preposition lam (for), as a warning that it deserves increased aversion, because everyone shrinks from being associated with it in any expression whatsoever. If one shrinks from it even with the beloved expression, how then will his state be with other than it?

When the opportunity of encouragement to obedience and warning against disobedience had been seized, He joined the second threat with the particle fa (then), indicating that after the victory of the Children of Israel over the people of the first occasion, and perhaps also indicating that its term was near the term of the reversal of fortune. So He said (Exalted is He): ﴿So when the promise of the Hereafter comes﴾; that is, comes in a manner that is like being compelled to it by force, contrary to what the one who comes to them wishes; ﴿the promise of the Hereafter﴾; that is, its time.
