﴿Or a creation﴾ — other than these — ﴿of what is greater﴾, i.e., what is greatly magnified, ﴿in your breasts﴾, regarding its acceptance of life, even if it were death, so that you may know how your condition would be in responding to what He wills concerning the resurrection (al-i'ada). For all of it originates from dust. So He who gave preference to your clay — the clay from which you were created — over the rest of clay, by growth, then by life, then by speech, and who gave some of the speaking beings preference over others with countless endowments, is able to transfer that excellence to clay, which He has transferred stage after stage until He made it a stone or iron. ﴿So they will say﴾, persisting in mockery: ﴿"Who will restore us?"﴾ — if we are such as that. ﴿Say: "He who originated you﴾, i.e., began your creation, ﴿the first time﴾, when you were nothing. He will restore you by the power with which He began you. Just as that power was not incapable of initiating, it is not incapable of restoring."

﴿So they will shake﴾, i.e., nodding with a promise that admits no failure, ﴿their heads toward you﴾, i.e., moving them out of extreme astonishment and mockery, as though, in the extremity of their ignorance, they had the utmost insight into what they are saying. And "al-nughd" and "al-in'ghad" mean movement up and down. (p-440) ﴿And they say﴾, mockingly: ﴿"When will it be?"﴾ Then he joined to it His saying (exalted is He): ﴿Say﴾ — in the manner of one who is moderate, neither vexed by their condition nor constricted by their words: ﴿"It may be that it is﴾, i.e., a happening from which there is no escape, ﴿near"﴾ — indicating the possibility of its occurrence, without certainty.

Then he resumed with a jussive (*jāzim*) construction in his words: ﴿on the day﴾; that is, it will be on the day when ﴿He calls you﴾; that is, the caller will call out to you from His side, by the blast (*nafkha*) or by other than it, such as saying: "O people of the graves, rise up for the recompense," or something similar. ﴿And you will respond﴾; that is, you will comply with the caller, doing what he intended by his call, seeking to answer him, and bringing it about. Or he used the words *du'ā'* (calling) and *istijāba* (responding) metaphorically for the resurrection (*ba'th*) and the rising (*inbi'āth*), to alert to the speed of both and the ease of their occurrence. Or the purpose of both is the bringing forth for the reckoning. ﴿With His praise﴾; that is, with His encompassing—glorified is He—of everything in power and knowledge, without any failure at all, but rather to the utmost of submission, as the form *istaf'ala* indicates. And you, with the speed of your response, will be praising God (exalted is He); that is, you will ascribe to Him the attribute of perfection. ﴿And you will think﴾, along with your responding and the length of your stay, ﴿that you remained only a little﴾; that is, "if not" (*in* meaning *mā*), ﴿you remained﴾ dead, ﴿but a little﴾, because of the severity of the terrors you see which surround you, and which confront you; or out of your ignorance of the realities of matters, as is your state today, as you see from the freshness of your creation and the lack of its change.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 53:

When He, glorified is He, commanded him to convey this speech, which contains such mockery of them, such rebuke of them, and such contempt for their intellects, that its full measure is known only to those like them among the eloquent and the pure Arabs, and since it was the speech of One who knows the outcomes and is aware of what the hearts conceal, the believers may often have followed its pattern and addressed them in similar terms of their own. So He forbade them from that, lest they say what stirs up evil or provokes harm. He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And say﴾; that is, say to them that, from wisdom and good admonition. And say ﴿to My servants﴾; that is, those who are fit to be attributed to Me, admonishing them, lest they go beyond the limit out of the intensity of their anger at the polytheists, if you say that to them. ﴿They should say﴾ the admonition, the wisdom, and the argument ﴿that which is best﴾, so that I may be with them, for I am with those who are God-fearing and those who do good. Then He gave the reason for that in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Satan﴾; that is, the one far from mercy, scorched by the curse, ﴿incites [discord] between them﴾; that is, he corrupts, stirs up, and whispers. The root of "nazgh" (incitement, provocation) is a thrust or a jab. They are not infallible, so they are likely to ﴿say﴾ things that do not suit the situation or the time, by mentioning the faults of others or their own virtues, and thus he brings about evil. Then He gave the reason for this reason in His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Satan has always been﴾; that is, from ancient times and from the origin of nature, a disposition with which he is created, ﴿to mankind an enemy﴾; that is, of intense enmity, ﴿clear﴾.

Then he explained "that which is best" — what their Lord had taught them of fairness — by His saying (exalted is He): ﴿Your Lord knows you best﴾. Then he resumed, saying (exalted is He): ﴿If He wills﴾ mercy for you, ﴿He will have mercy upon you﴾, by making the acts of goodness easy for you; ﴿or if He wills﴾ punishment for you, ﴿He will punish you﴾, by making you easy for the acts of evil. So when they are told this, they are deserving of presenting their deeds — or those of them whom God wills — to what they know of good and evil, so that they consider which of the two is nearer to them. Perhaps this would turn them back from corruption within themselves, to cut off the root of obstinacy. It is also permissible — and this is, in my view, the better — that the verse be a resumed statement occupying the position of a reason for the command to speak in the best manner. That is: ﴿Your Lord knows you best﴾, O servants, and what your affairs will come to, of happiness and misery; ﴿if He wills, He will have mercy upon you﴾ by guiding you; ﴿or if He wills, He will punish you﴾ by leading you astray. So do not despise, O believers, the polytheists, by being certain that they are among the people of the Fire and thus reproaching them with that, for this leads to enmities, burning of breasts and rage of hearts, to no benefit, because the final outcome is unknown. And do not go beyond, regarding them, what I command you, in speech and action, for that is the best. Then He elevated the address to the highest of creation and the head of the people of the Sharia, so that those below him would be more entitled to the meaning than he: He (exalted is He) said: ﴿And We have not sent you﴾ — that is, We have not sent you except to call with the like of that, according to what We command you. And ﴿We have not sent you﴾ — that is, along with what We possess of greatness, self-sufficient beyond everything — ﴿over them as a guardian﴾, that is, a keeper and a guarantor for others of what pleases God. Rather, We have sent you only as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, so be gentle with them, and command your companions to be gentle with them.

(p. 444) When He commanded them to attribute knowledge of them to Him, glorified is He, He informed them of something more general than that. So He said, exalted is He, conjoining it to "your Lord" to inform them that His knowledge is not restricted to them but encompasses everything. He addressed the Prophet, the most knowledgeable of creation about Him, glorified is He, restricting the address to him, to indicate that no one else knows this with its true knowledge: ﴿And your Lord﴾, that is, the One who has been good to you by making you the most perfect of creation, ﴿is most knowing﴾, that is, more than any knower, ﴿of those in the heavens﴾, that is, all of them, ﴿and the earth﴾, including both humans and others, ﴿of their conditions, their measures, their terms, and what each of them deserves, because He is the One who created them and differentiated among them in their characters and their states. So how do they find it far-fetched that the orphan of Abu Talib, as they used to say, should be a prophet, or that his companions, the naked and the hungry, should be better than them?

Since it has been understood from this context that some things are preferred over others, (p. 444) until the Spirit becomes receptive to life, both at the beginning and in return, and since it has been understood from the beginning of the surah and the end of the one before it that some prophets are singled out for virtues of the spirit of knowledge and wisdom that no one else has attained, He stated this here. Exalted is He, He said, conjoining it to what the context of informing about knowledge indicated, turning to the station of greatness, which the situation calls for, namely the description of being most knowing: ﴿And We have certainly﴾, that is, We have distinguished among them with vices and virtues, preferring some of them over others according to the extent of Our knowledge of them and the comprehensiveness of Our power over them, in their fitness for happiness and misery. So We preferred some people over others: We preferred scholars over others, and We preferred prophets among them over others. Indeed, ﴿We preferred﴾, that is, by what We have of greatness, ﴿some of the prophets﴾, that is, whether they were messengers or not, ﴿over others﴾, after We had made all of them excellent, for the piety and goodness of each of them. So none of the Arabs, the Children of Israel, or others should deny Our preferring this noble Prophet, whom We opened the surah by preferring over all creation, for We do what We will by the complete power and comprehensive knowledge We possess. The summary is that among the greatest fruits of action is preference, by giving each one, indeed each thing, what it deserves. Through this, the perfection of His wisdom in the comprehensiveness of His knowledge and the completeness of His power is inferred. Therefore He mentioned preference here (p. 445) after mentioning absolute knowledge, and He explicitly stated the preference of the noblest of creation, and He omitted mention of others, just as He mentioned preference in this world after affirming knowledge restricted by sins, in His saying: ﴿Whoever desires the immediate [life]﴾ [al-Isra: 18], up to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿See how We have favored some of them over others﴾ [al-Isra: 21].

Since the address in this surah, both before and after this verse, is clearly directed to the Children of Israel, and the allusion to them is evident in many places, and since David, peace be upon him, was the one who founded al-Masjid al-Aqsa, to which the Night Journey took place, and since he had been especially given the softening of iron, which the polytheists were commanded to make into weapons in response to their denial of resurrection, and since he, despite being a king, was among the most humble of people, the most frequent in weeping, and the furthest from exultant pride on earth, He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We gave﴾, that is, by what We have of greatness, ﴿David﴾, that is, who was one of the followers of Moses, to whom We gave the Book and made it guidance for the Children of Israel, so that they would not take a guardian other than Me, ﴿the Psalms﴾. This is because they are certain that the prophets between Moses and Jesus, among the prophets of the Children of Israel, were below Moses in rank. Each of them called to his own law, acting by the ruling of the Torah, which God honored him with, not departing from any part of its sunnah. So the analogy (p. 446) would require that they be equal in virtue. But this did not happen according to the reasoning of people. Rather, glorified is He, He differentiated among them according to His knowledge of their conditions, even in revelation. He singled out David, peace be upon him, with a Book that is entirely admonitions, and admonitions are the thing most incompatible with walking on earth in exultant pride, and the strongest prohibition against it, and the greatest command to speak what is best, with sincerity, watchfulness (muraqabah), and goodness. Moreover, it contains glorification of everything, which is among the greatest aims of the surah, as the text of the Psalms regarding it was mentioned shortly before. So mentioning his preference through it here was the most fitting thing for this station. In this is the greatest allusion and the most significant reminder of the virtue of Bayt al-Maqdis, which He made a cause for the preference of prophets: sometimes through emigration to it, as with Abraham, peace be upon him; sometimes through the intention of purifying it from polytheism and illuminating it with monotheism, as with Moses, peace be upon him; sometimes through founding its structure and erecting its pillars, as with David, peace be upon him; and sometimes through the Night Journey to it, leading the prophets in prayer there, and ascending from it to the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary (Sidrat al-Muntaha) and the Exalted Station. As for his preference and the preference of his son Solomon, over our Prophet Muhammad and upon both of them be blessings and peace, through kingship and the vastness of authority, this falls under His saying, exalted is He: ﴿See how We have favored some of them over others﴾ [al-Isra: 21]. Al-Bukhari related in the Book of Tafsir (p. 447):

"From Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: 'Recitation was made light for David. He would order his mounts to be saddled, and he would finish reciting before they were saddled,' meaning the Qur'an."

Among the greatest reasons for mentioning David, peace be upon him, and his Psalms here is the mention of resurrection, the station of which is explicit in it. Likewise, the mention of the Fire, though the Torah is devoid of that. As for resurrection, there is no mention of it in the Torah at all. As for the Fire, nothing indicating it is mentioned, except "the Jahim" in one place. But the Psalms mention the Fire, the Abyss (al-Hawiyah), and the Jahim in more than one place. As for resurrection, it is explicitly stated there, and it is clear that it is with the spirit and the body. He said in the hundred and third Psalm: "Bless the LORD, O my soul; O LORD my God, thou art very great; thou art clothed with honour and majesty. Who coverest thyself with light as with a garment: who stretchest out the heavens like a curtain. Who layeth the beams of his chambers in the waters: who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind: Who maketh his angels spirits; his ministers a flaming fire. Who laid the foundations of the earth, that it should not be removed for ever. Thou coveredst it with the deep as with a garment: the waters stood above the mountains. At thy rebuke they fled; at the voice of thy thunder they hasted away. They go up by the mountains; they go down by the valleys unto the place which thou hast founded for them. Thou hast set a bound that they may not pass over; that they turn not again to cover the earth. He sendeth the springs into the valleys, which run among the hills. They give drink to every beast of the field: the wild asses quench their thirst. By them shall the fowls of the heaven have their habitation, which sing among the branches. ... O LORD, how manifold are thy works! in wisdom hast thou made them all: the earth is full of thy riches. So is this great and wide sea, wherein are things creeping innumerable, both small and great beasts. There go the ships: there is that leviathan, whom thou hast made to play therein. These wait all upon thee; that thou mayest give them their meat in due season. That thou givest them they gather: thou openest thine hand, they are filled with good. Thou hidest thy face, they are troubled: thou takest away their breath, they die, and return to their dust. Thou sendest forth thy spirit, they are created: and thou renewest the face of the earth. The glory of the LORD shall endure for ever." End of quotation.

So this is a response to anyone who might say to the Arabs, from among the Jews, that the matter is as you say, that there is no resurrection, as some of their heretics say, as was mentioned of them in the text of the Gospel, and as was reported of them in Surat an-Nisa, that they said: "You are better guided in the way than the believers" [an-Nisa: 51], and "Your religion is better than the religion of Muhammad." In the Psalms, as mentioned at the beginning of the surah, from the Torah of Moses, peace be upon him: (p. 449) "that you should not take a guardian other than God." This is among the greatest aims of the surah. In the hundred and forty-fifth Psalm he said: "Put not your trust in princes, nor in the son of man, in whom there is no help. His breath goes forth, he returns to his earth; in that very day his thoughts perish."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 56:

When He had established that it is His (exalted be He) prerogative to do that and similar things, namely bestowing preference and effecting transformation, in accordance with His knowledge and His power, it became established beyond any doubt that there is no refuge except in Him. Therefore He commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to confirm this by telling them to say what would make manifest the powerlessness of their associates. This was a refutation of their saying: "We are not fit to worship Him directly, so we worship some of the near ones so that they may intercede for us with Him." So He (exalted be He) said: ﴿Say: Call upon those﴾, and He indicated the weakness of their intellects and their lack of firm reasoning by using the word "claim" when He said: ﴿you claim﴾, that they are gods. He made clear the lowliness of their rank by His saying (exalted be He): ﴿besides Him﴾, meaning: other than Him, such as the angels, Uzayr, al-Masih, and the idols, ﴿to bring you some good or to ward off some harm from you﴾. ﴿Then they have no power﴾, meaning: whether you call upon them or do not call upon them, they do not possess ﴿the removal of the harm﴾, meaning: the distress which by its nature afflicts the whole body, ﴿from you﴾, so that it does not leave any part of it, ﴿nor any transformation﴾ of it from one state to something lighter than it. This is far from being able to replace it with a good state, or to turn it upon your enemy. The verse is similar to His saying (exalted be He): ﴿So you have no ability to avert or to help﴾ [al-Furqan: 19]. How then could any of them be taken as a guardian apart from Me?

They said: The occasion of its revelation was the complaint of Quraysh to the Prophet (ﷺ) about the drought that befell them, when he invoked against them with seven years like the seven years of Yusuf (peace be upon him).

The word ﴿يَمْلِكُونَ﴾ ("they possess") was not put in the accusative (as it could have been), lest it be thought that the negation is caused by the supplication, and thus be restricted to it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 57:

When he had made clear that they have no power to harm or to benefit, he made clear that they compete with one another to draw near to Him, hoping that He will benefit them and fearing that He will harm them. So He (exalted is He) said: ﴿Those﴾; that is, those who have raised their ranks by turning to the obedience of Allah. The polytheists raised their ranks by deifying their gods. He expressed this by describing the subject (*mubtada'*, the grammatical subject) with His words (exalted is He): ﴿who call upon﴾; that is, whom the disbelievers call upon and deify. Then He gave the predicate about the subject (*mubtada'*) with His words (exalted is He): ﴿seek﴾; that is, they strive with great striving; ﴿to their Lord﴾, the One who does good to them, alone; ﴿the means﴾; that is, the station, the rank, and the nearness through righteous deeds; ﴿as to which of them would be nearest﴾; that is, they compete through deeds, in a competition where each of them seeks to be nearer to Him and more excellent in His sight; ﴿and they hope for His mercy﴾, out of desire for what is with Him; ﴿and they fear His punishment﴾, out of glorification of His majesty. Among them are those who are accountable, such as the angels, the Messiah, and ʿUzayr, in actuality; and others, such as idols, in potentiality, insofar as He is able to create in them the power of perception for obedience and for punishment, so that they would be like that. Therefore, those who worship them are more deserving that they should worship Him and seek the means to Him.

Al-Bukhari related in the Book of Tafsir, from ʿAbd Allah (may Allah be pleased with him), concerning ﴿seek to their Lord the means﴾, that he said: "There were some people from mankind who used to worship some people from the jinn; then the jinn embraced Islam, and these people held fast to their religion."

Then He gave a general reason for their fear, so He (exalted is He) said: ﴿Indeed, the punishment of your Lord﴾; that is, the One who does good to you by lifting from your community the vengeance of total annihilation; ﴿is﴾; that is, as a constant state inherent in Him; ﴿something to be feared﴾; that is, deserving to be guarded against by everyone, whether a near angel or a sent prophet, let alone others, because of what has been witnessed of His destruction of generations and of His great works.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (*Nazm al-Durar*) on surah 17, verse 58:

Since the meaning is: "So beware of Us; for We have destroyed the earlier nations and laid waste to the fortified towns," He (exalted is He) connected to it His words ﴿And not﴾; that is, "and not" (وما, *wa-ma*). He intensified the negation, so He said (exalted is He): ﴿any town﴾, from the towns, this one in which you are and others, ﴿except that We will destroy it﴾, that is, by virtue of the majesty that is Ours, ﴿before the Day of Resurrection﴾ or ﴿punish it with a severe punishment﴾, by some kind of destruction, because of the disbelief or disobedience they are upon. It is narrated from Muqatil that this is general: for the righteous by death, and for the wicked by punishment. (p-452)

Since the contingent (*al-mumkin*, the technical term for what may or may not exist) has in itself nothing but non-existence, and that [non-existence] encompasses the time before [its existence], He omitted the preposition (*al-jarr*) and said (exalted is He): ﴿before the Day of Resurrection﴾, which you deny, just as We did with Bayt al-Maqdis in the two instances mentioned at the beginning of the surah, for the corruption of its people. So beware of the like of that. ﴿Or punish it﴾, that is, the town, by punishing its people, ﴿with a severe punishment﴾, while it remains standing.

Since He emphasized this with the nominal sentence (*al-jumlah al-ismiyyah*, a sentence beginning with a noun), He increased its emphasis in answer to one who seems to say: "Is there any exception to this?" For the like of this scarcely seems credible. So He said (exalted is He): ﴿That was﴾, that is, this great matter, ﴿in the Book﴾, which is with Us, ﴿inscribed﴾ in the form of a report. Reports are not subject to *naskh* (abrogation, the technical term for a later ruling canceling an earlier one). So if there were no gathering, Our command would be fit to be obeyed, out of fear of Our might. And it is inevitable that We will frighten you after your long security and destroy many of your mighty ones at the hand of this one man, whom you all conspire against and whose command you disdain, although We sent him for your honour and the elevation of your renown. It is also inevitable that We will bring him into this land of yours with troops (p-453) possessing mighty strength, for your corruption in it and your disdain for him, just as We did to the Children of Israel when they corrupted their sanctuary, as has passed.

The Imam, the memorizer (*al-hafiz*) Abu 'Amr 'Uthman ibn Sa'id al-Dani, said in *Kitab al-Fitan*: 'Abd ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Harawi narrated to us in his book: 'Umar ibn Ahmad ibn 'Uthman ibn Shahin narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Harun al-Hadrami narrated to us: 'Ali ibn 'Abd Allah al-Tamimi narrated to us: 'Abd al-Mun'im ibn Idris narrated to us, saying: my father informed us, from Wahb ibn Munabbih, who said: "The Jazira is safe from ruin until Armenia is ruined; Armenia is safe from ruin until Egypt is ruined; Egypt is safe from ruin until Kufa is ruined; and the Great Battle will not occur until Kufa is ruined. When the Great Battle occurs, Constantinople will be conquered at the hands of a man of the Banu Hashim. The ruin of al-Andalus will come from the direction of the Zanj; the ruin of Ifriqiya from the direction of al-Andalus; the ruin of Egypt from the cutting off of the Nile and the disputes of the armies within it; the ruin of Iraq from hunger and the sword; the ruin of Kufa from an enemy behind them who will belittle them, until they cannot drink a single drop of the Euphrates; the ruin of Basra from the direction of Iraq; the ruin of Aylah from an enemy who will drive them, at times by land and at times by sea; the ruin of al-Rayy from the direction of the Daylam; the ruin of Khurasan from the direction of Tibet; the ruin of Tibet from the direction of China; the ruin of China from the direction of India; the ruin of Yemen from locusts and the sultan; the ruin of Makkah from the direction of Abyssinia; the ruin of Madinah from hunger."' 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Khalid narrated to us: 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Nusayr narrated to us: Muhammad ibn Khalaf narrated to us: Salim ibn Janada informed us: my father informed us, from Hisham ibn 'Urwa, from his father, from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The last town of the towns of Islam to be ruined will be Madinah." End of quotation. Al-Tirmidhi also reported it through this chain.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 59:

Since the disbelievers of Quraysh kept repeating their demands for signs after their harm had grown severe, and since he (ﷺ), because of his intense eagerness for the faith of every person, how much more for his own people, the Arabs, and how much more for his paternal cousins among them, may have wished that Allah (Exalted) would answer them with their proposal, hoping for their faith and to relieve him and his followers of their harm, and since what they had witnessed of the sign of the Night Journey was a dazzling matter, and then they did not believe, rather some of those among them who had believed apostatized, the situation strongly called for it to be said, after mention of the sign of punishment: "Why is their punishment not hastened, or why are they not granted their proposals, so that the matter may be decided?" So the answer is given: What prevented Us from hastening their punishment is only that We have set for them a term that must be reached. ﴿And nothing prevented Us﴾, that is, with the greatness We possess, which nothing can overcome and no one can hinder; ﴿from sending﴾, that is, a sending that manifests Our greatness, in a general manner; ﴿with the signs﴾, that is, those which Quraysh proposed; so it was as if they had no signs except these; ﴿except﴾ Our knowledge, in the world of witnessing, of what has occurred ﴿that the former peoples denied them﴾, that is, the proposals; and Our knowledge, in the world of the unseen, that these people are like the former ones, in that the wretched among them does not believe in the proposals, just as he did not believe in other things, and that he says about them what he said about other things, namely that they are sorcery and the like; whereas the blessed one does not need them for his faith. How many nations have We answered with their proposals, and that only increased the people of misguidance among them in disbelief? So We seized them, because Our way is that We do not give respite after answering the proposals to those who deny them. We have decreed, out of mercy toward this community and its honoring above the earlier nations, that it not be annihilated, because from the loins of its disbelievers there will come forth sincere servants of Ours. The negation here is an emphatic form, meant to deny that they would be answered in their proposals, and it may not be taken literally, because it indicates the existence of something that makes the act impossible for one who is able to perform it. Then it is joined to what the context indicates, namely: "How many have We answered?", to the end of what I mentioned; the saying of Him (Exalted): ﴿And We gave﴾, that is, with the dazzling might We possess, ﴿Thamud the she-camel﴾, being ﴿visible﴾, that is, illuminating, worthy that whoever witnesses it should gain insight through it; ﴿but they wronged themselves through it﴾, that is, they fell into wrongdoing, which is like darkness, because of it, by not believing and not fearing its consequence. He specified the sign of Thamud for mention as a warning, because they were Arabs who proposed what had been the cause of the destruction of their own kind, and because they had knowledge of it, and of its dwellings, owing to its nearness to them and its being in their lands, which they did not have of other signs. He specified the she-camel because it is an animal that He brought forth from a rock; and the context is to establish the power of resurrection, even if they were stones or iron; and it indicated their folly in both matters, by way of disordered arrangement, by mentioning David (peace be upon him), as an allusion to iron, and the she-camel as an allusion to stones. So to Allah belongs this allusion: how subtle it is! And this expression: how sublime and how true it is! ﴿And We do not send﴾, that is, with the majesty We possess, before which mountains melt, ﴿the signs﴾, that is, the proposals and others, ﴿except as a warning﴾, that is, to those to whom they are sent; so if they fear, they are saved, and otherwise they perish. When the matter is revealed to you in the world of witnessing, that they do not fear them, in accordance with what was with Us in the world of the unseen, it becomes known that there is no benefit for you in them.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 60:**

Since the reasoning is the matching of one statement to another, the sense is: "Recall that We said to you: ﴿Indeed, those upon whom the word of your Lord has been justified will not believe﴾ [Yunus 10:96] ﴿Even if every sign should come to them﴾ [Yunus 10:97]; and recall what has occurred of that in the past, from the signs of the earlier peoples, and in the present, from the story of the Night Journey (al-Isra')." Then He connected to it His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And [recall] when﴾, that is, recall when, ﴿We said﴾, by the all-encompassing majesty We possess, ﴿to you, "Indeed your Lord﴾, who bestows favor upon you through kindness, by being gentle with your community, ﴿has encompassed the people﴾ in knowledge and power. You will find this, if you apply some of it to others, to be a matter of perfect order, exact as the feathers of an arrow, without any discrepancy. Know that He is your protector against them, your shield, and the one who will make your religion prevail, as He promised you." Then He connected, upon His saying "And We do not send [signs] except...", His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you﴾, that is, by what We possess of overwhelming might, which has absolute sufficiency, ﴿except as a trial﴾, that is, a test and an examination, ﴿for the people﴾, so that by it there would become evident, in the world of witnessing, the God-fearing who does good and the ignorant who does evil, just as it is with Us in the world of the unseen. Thereby We establish the proof against them, not so that anyone among those upon whom the Word has been justified would believe, nor so that We would increase in knowledge of their inner selves. There is no doubt that the story of the Night Journey to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), and then to the highest heavens, was while awake and not in a dream, by the definitive, mass-transmitted evidence, from [the refutation of] the one who denied it and the apostasy of the one who apostatized. This is the position of the majority (al-Jumhur) and of the People of the Sunnah and the Community (Ahl al-Sunnah wa'l-Jama'ah). Countless reports have come down attesting to its authenticity; this is the transmitted account. As for rational possibility, it is established and needs no explanation, for every atom of existing things contains wonders, marvels, subtleties and delicate refinements at which minds are astonished. But since it accords with custom, natures have become accustomed to it, so eyes and ears do not reject it. As for something like this, since it is contrary to custom, it has been regarded as strange by the weak of mind, whose understanding does not exceed what is perceptible, according to the customs to which they are accustomed. But as for the people of intellect (Uli'l-Albab), who are safe from the promptings of Satan and the whisperings of custom, and who look with the eyes of insight upon the traces of God's mercy in the fashioning of created things and the bringing into being of innovated things, in the dominion and the realm of the sovereignty (Malakut), in the witnessed and the unseen, in creation and command, they acknowledge it, and that it is among the greatest signs and the most brilliant wondrous proofs. The clearest proof of this is His saying, "as a trial", for if it had been a dream, no one would have found it strange, and so it would not have been a trial. Perhaps He named it a "vision", which is [properly] for a dream, by way of comparison and metaphor, because of the extraordinary matters in it, which are more fitting to a dream in the ordinary course of things. Al-Bukhari reported in the Book of Tafsir, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, concerning ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you﴾, the verse, that he said: "It is a vision of the eye, which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was shown on the night he was taken on the Night Journey."

Since everything whose cause is hidden and which departs from custom is a trial, by which whoever has the truth in his nature and whoever has falsehood in his nature is known, and whoever has a sound natural disposition (fitrah) and whoever has it reversed, and since He had reported that the tree of al-Zaqqum (the bitter tree) grows at the root of Hell (al-Jahim), and that was in utmost strangeness, He joined it to the Night Journey in this matter. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And the cursed tree in the Qur'an﴾, connected to "the vision", by its being harmful, for the Arabs call everything harmful "cursed", and because it is in the abode of the curse, and everyone who has intellect wants to keep far from it. And it is, as al-Bukhari reported in the Book of Tafsir, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, the tree of al-Zaqqum. We also made it a trial for the people, by which We establish the proof against them in disbelief and in faith, so that We make firm those among them whom We wish to believe, by the first, which is the Night Journey, ﴿and We warn them﴾, by the second and its like, ﴿but it only increases them﴾, that is, the disbelievers among them, in the warning, at the time of the warning; so what follows it of times yet to come is more deserving of increase, ﴿in nothing but grave transgression﴾, that is, overstepping the bounds, which is of the utmost greatness. So they say of the first what has preceded at the beginning of the surah, and of the second: "Muhammad says that the fuel of the Fire is people and stones, then he says that there are trees in it, and you know that fire burns trees." They did not say what they are most knowledgeable of, namely that He who made for them fire from green trees is able to place trees in the Fire. Among the most appropriate things to recall here is what was mentioned by the scholar, the shaykh of our shaykhs, Zayn al-Din Abu Bakr ibn al-Husayn al-Maraghi, in his lexicon (Mu'jam al-'Ayn), the Madinan, in the History of the Noble City (Madinah), at the beginning of the fourth chapter, in the mention of the valleys. He said: "Wadi al-Shazat (with two pointed letters, both with fatha) comes from the east of Madinah, from places far from it, until it reaches the barrier which the fire of al-Harra created, which erupted in Jumada al-Akhirah in the year six hundred and fifty-four" (meaning: that which is alluded to by the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "The Hour will not come until a fire comes out of the Hijaz, by which the necks of camels in Busra will be illuminated"). He said: "Its emergence was from a valley called Uhayliyyin in the eastern harra, and from its place of exit it moved toward the north for a period of three months, creeping like the crawling of ants, eating whatever mountain or stone it passed over, but not eating trees, so it does not pass over anything of that kind without becoming a barrier through which there is no path for a person or an animal, up to the end of the harra toward the north." Then he related the story, and it is a strange one; and in it he transmitted, citing al-Matari, concerning what relates to its not harming wood.

Since what preceded: they deemed the return (to life) unlikely because they would become crumbled remains (rufat) after death. He (exalted) informed them of His power over that. Even if they were to become something harder for them to restore than crumbled remains, such as stones or iron, He indicated His power to act beyond the customary order (khariq al-'ada, the breaking of habit) with iron, by softening it for one of His servants. Then, with stones, by way of ascending progression in the disordered spreading (nashr mushawwash, a rhetorical sequence of scattered items), with what is more wondrous than that, which is the bestowing of life upon them for another of His servants. He indicated His acting upon dust, which is the final state of crumbled remains, and which led them to deem it unlikely, with what is more wondrous than everything that preceded it. This is by bestowing complete life, with speech, upon it (p-462) without any prior state of life at all. This is by the creation of Adam, peace be upon him, who is their origin. Along with this there is a preservation of the context through consolation: that signs do not benefit one who is decreed to wretchedness; and that Adam, peace be upon him, was subjected to the envier, and his harm toward him intensified, although he was the chosen one of God and the first of His prophets. Together with clarification, because the most common cause of transgression is envy, which moved Iblis to what he did. So He (exalted) said: ﴿And when﴾; that is: and remember also what occurred of transgression, despite seeing the signs, at the beginning of this existence, from Iblis, who is among the most knowledgeable of creation of God's signs and His greatness; then from those who followed him among the descendants of Adam, peace be upon him, after the enmity had been established, in opposing their Lord who was good to them, along with claiming his guardianship. ﴿We said﴾; that is: by the greatness that is ours, whose intended will nothing disobeys; ﴿to the angels﴾, when We created your father Adam and gave him preference: ﴿Prostrate to Adam﴾, in compliance with My command; ﴿so they prostrated, except Iblis﴾, who refused to prostrate, because he was among those upon whom the Word had been realized; and what he knew of God's power and greatness did not benefit him. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿He said﴾; that is: to Us, denying, arrogant; ﴿Shall I prostrate to one whom You created﴾; that is: in humility; ﴿from clay﴾ (p-463) ﴿clay﴾, whose origin is clay. So he disbelieved by attributing to Us injustice and lack of wisdom, imagining that he was more noble than Adam, peace be upon him, on the ground that branches return to roots, and that fire, which is his origin, is more noble than clay. He overlooked that clay is more beneficial than fire, and so it is more noble. Moreover, even by way of supposition, all substances are of one genus, and God (exalted), who brought them into existence from nothingness, preferences some of them over others by the accidents He brings about in them, as the indication of this was previously mentioned in: ﴿And We have certainly preferred some of the prophets over others﴾ [al-Isra: 55].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 62:

When (Exalted is He) informed of his arrogance, it was as if it were said: "This is indeed a great impudence and a boldness against the Most High Court. Was there anything other than this?" It was said: "Yes. ﴿He said, 'Tell me, is this the one whom You have honoured above me?'﴾ That is: inform me, ﴿this one whom You have honoured above me﴾, by what did You honour him over me, despite his weakness and my strength?" It was as if it were said: "He has gone to the extreme in discourtesy. What came after this?" It was said: "He swore, [an oath] to emphasize the improbability that anyone would dare such boldness toward the Supreme King: ﴿'If You give me respite﴾, that is, O Supreme King, a lengthy respite, ﴿'until the Day of Resurrection,'﴾ alive and empowered, ﴿'I will surely seize control of﴾, that is, through misguidance, ﴿his descendants,﴾ that is, I will surely dominate them ﴿with the severity of my cunning, as the eater dominates what he has taken in his jaw (p-464) by Your empowering me over them,﴾ ﴿'except for a few.'﴾ and they are Your allies, whom You have protected from me."

So it is as if it was said: "He has persisted in defiance. What did his Lord say to him after the third time?" It was said: ﴿He said﴾, threatening him; ﴿Go﴾, i.e., proceed to the respite you have mentioned, by My will and not by My command, for you will not transgress Our decree concerning you. We have decreed your wretchedness and the wretchedness of those whom We wish to obey you. Therefore He follows this with His statement (exalted is He): ﴿whoever follows you﴾, i.e., even the slightest following, ﴿of them﴾, i.e., of the children of Adam (peace be upon him). It is also possible that by the bare verb is meant that whoever follows him without any treatment of his original nature (fitrah, the primordial disposition) will not be but deeply rooted in evil.

Since the implied meaning is "I have made him taste of your disgrace," He expressed it with His statement: ﴿indeed Hell﴾, i.e., the fiery stratum in which one is met with scowling, ﴿is your recompense﴾, i.e., your recompense and their recompense; you will be repaid this ﴿as a full recompense﴾, complete, perfect and sufficient, in accordance with what you deserve for your evil deeds.

The root و ف ر (wafara), in all its permutations, which are fifteen, is distributed as follows. Six are of the waw type: wafara, warafa, fawara, farawa, rafawa, rawafa. Three are of the yā' type: farayā, rafayā, rayafa. Six are of the hamzated type (hamz, the glottal stop): raf'a, ra'afa, fara'a, fa'ara, afara, arafa. They all revolve around abundance, exceeding a limit, rising above a measure, and surplus beyond sufficiency. Thus al-wafr is a large place. A siqā' wafr (a waterskin) is one from which nothing of its hide has been lost. An idāwa wafrā' (a water vessel) is a large one. Al-wafra is hair that reaches the ears. Al-wāfir is a type of prosodic meter ('arūḍ, the science of Arabic poetic metres), whose pattern is mufā'alatun repeated six times. Al-wafr is wealth. Min al-māl means abundant and vast, and al-'āmm min kulli shay' means the general or broad part of everything. Waffarahu tawfīran means he multiplied it. Wafara lahu 'irḍahu means he did not insult him. Waffara 'aṭā'ahu means he returned his gift to him while he was content. Waffarahu tawfīran also means he completed it and made it full, because perfection is hardly realised except with an increase. Al-thawb means he cut the garment wide. Al-wāfira is the ram's rump when it is large, and also the world, life, and every elongated piece of fat. Hum mutawāfirūn means there is abundance among them. Istawfara 'alayhi ḥaqqahu means he took his right in full.

Warafa al-nabtu yarifu means that when you see brightness in the plant from its moisture. This happens only from its freshness, its spreading, and its being pleasing to the eye. Warafa al-ẓillu yarifu warfan, wariīfan, wurūfan means the shade expanded, lengthened and extended, like awrafa and warraffa. Al-warf is the thin part of the sides of the liver, due to its increase and slackness. Al-rifa, on the pattern of 'idah, is the fresh plant. Warraftuhu tawrīfan means I sucked it. Warraftu al-arḍ means I divided the land, as if this were a form of removal.

Fārat al-qidr means the pot boiled until what is in it rose and overflowed. Every hot thing fāra fawran. Fāra al-'irq means the vein swelled; al-Qāmūs (the dictionary al-Qāmūs al-Muḥīṭ) adds that it also means to strike. Fāra al-misk means the musk spread out. Fārat al-ibil means the odour of camels' hides when they are moistened after being watered. Al-fā'ir is an animal whose nerves are prominent. Ataw min fawrihim means they came immediately, or came before they had settled, because their movement is an expansion and spreading, so it was called fawr. Al-fār is a person's muscle, because it is thicker than what lies beneath it. Al-fūr, with a ḍamma, means gazelles, the plural of fā'ir, because it is among the swiftest animals in fleeing, the most powerful in leaping, and the widest in running. Al-Qazzāz (the lexicographer al-Qazzaz) said: al-fāra and al-fūra are a wind in the fetlock of a horse, which puffs up when rubbed and gathers when left alone. He said of fa'ara that when it is touched it puffs up. He repeated this in al-Qāmūs under the hamzated roots, saying: al-fa'ra is for the male of the known animal and for the female, and it is also a wind in the animal's fetlock which puffs up when rubbed and gathers when left, like al-fūra with a ḍamma. Al-fūr is the young of a donkey, because of its lightness and the swiftness of its movement and leaping. Fawwārtā al-kirsh (the two paunch glands) are two glands within two pieces of flesh. It was also said that al-fawwāra is the flesh within which the gland is found, and it was said that they exist in every fleshy animal, due to the necessity of increase, whether we say they are flesh or gland. Al-Qazzāz said: they say that a man's semen falls into the kidney, then into the fawwāra, then into the testicle; so it was named fawwāra because it ejects what is in it into the testicle.

Al-fīrān, with a kasra, are two pieces of iron that flank the tongue of a balance, because they are wider than the tongue. Al-fīra, with a kasra, whether with a hamza or without, is dates that are boiled, mashed, and cooked with fenugreek (ḥulba), which a woman who has just given birth drinks; this is what al-Qazzāz said. In Mukhtaṣar al-'Ayn (the abridgment of al-'Ayn, a lexicon), it is said: fenugreek that is boiled; when it boils and its foam is produced, the foam is put into a press and then strained, and women after childbirth drink it. He repeated this in al-Qāmūs under the hamzated roots and said: al-fi'ara with a kasra, al-fu'ara like thumāma, al-fa'īra, and al-fi'ara like 'inaba, and its hamza may be left out, are fenugreek boiled for women after childbirth. It was named either because of its boiling or because of its expansion, by the gathering of dates and fenugreek.

Al-far and al-farwa are a known garment, named for the emergence of its wool and the increase of gentleness in it, as if it were the origin of the whole root. Farwat al-ra's is the scalp with its hair. Al-farwa is white land with no plants, because it is wider for it in this condition. Al-farwa also means wealth and abundance; a dry bunch of gathered plants; a robe whose sleeves were rolled up, since without their increase they would not have been rolled up; half of a cloak made of camel hair, as if it were likened to al-farwa because of the length of its wool; a bag in which the beggar places his charity; the crown, for its width, height and completeness, and for the wealth of its owner; and a woman's headscarf, for its excess over what she needs, its fullness, and its surplus over her head.

Rafā al-thawb yarfūhu means he repaired it and mended its tear. Al-Qāmūs mentions it under the hamzated roots and says: he joined part of it to another part. Al-Qazzāz said: the hamzated form is more common. Al-ri'ā', on the pattern of kisā', means joining, gathering and agreement. From it comes what is said to a newly married man: bi'l-rifā' wa'l-banīn (may it be with harmony and children). They also repeated it under the hamzated roots, and al-Qāmūs says: that is, with joining and the gathering of the scattered. Al-Qazzāz said: the meaning of rafā is that he married. Al-arfā means one with large ears that are slack. Al-Qazzāz said: al-udhun al-rafwā' (the ear that is rafwā') is the one that turns towards the other until their tips almost touch. Rafawtu al-rajul means I calmed the man when he was terrified. This was repeated in al-Qāmūs under the hamzated roots, because that is more expansive for his thought, since it is more soothing to his eye.

Al-rawf means calm. It is wider than agitation, because it occurs only from the rest of the eye. Al-Qāmūs says: it is not from al-ra'fa (mercy). Al-rawfa is mercy. Rāfa yarāfu is a dialect form of ra'fa yar'afu. Its remainder will come shortly, God willing (exalted is He).

When He - glorified is He - began with the threat, out of kindness to those who are accountable (al-mukallafin, those upon whom the obligations of the law fall), He followed His saying "Go" with His saying, giving an example of His power to dominate whoever He misleads, with a cavalry raid that struck a people. It cried out at them with a cry that would drive them from their dwellings, uproot them from their positions, and rally against them its troops, both horse and foot, until it wiped them out: ﴿And incite﴾, i.e., make light of; and "al-fazz" (incitement) originally means cutting, i.e., cause him to slip by cutting him off from what is right. So said al-Rummani. ﴿Those among them whom you can﴾, and they are those over whom We have given you power. ﴿With your voice﴾, i.e., your calling with singing and flutes and everything you adorn with whisperings. ﴿And rally﴾, i.e., gather, or drive with the utmost of the shouting you can muster. ﴿Against them with your horsemen﴾, i.e., the riders of your army. ﴿And your foot soldiers﴾, i.e., those who go on foot among them. The meaning: do everything you are able to do, and leave nothing of your strength unused, for you have no power over anything I have not decreed for you.

Since Satan seeks to share with people in all their affairs, through his whisperings that drive them to corrupt those affairs, if they obey him they become those who seek to make him a partner, even if they have no awareness of that; so He expressed it with the form of mutual participation (mufa'alah), and said (exalted is He): ﴿And share with them﴾, i.e., by your leaping into mixing with them when they share with you in doing what agrees with your desire. ﴿In wealth﴾, i.e., that which they strive to acquire. ﴿And children﴾, i.e., those whom they beget, if they acquire them through a forbidden means, or do not mention My name over them; likewise their sacrifices made to other than God, their spending on forbidden things, and their teaching their children sins and disbelief, as a sharing in them. ﴿And promise them﴾, i.e., of the false promises, that which makes them light-headed and deceives them: the intercession of the gods, honour with God (exalted is He), delaying repentance, and the like. Then He turned to His righteous servants and informed them, to strengthen them and to alert others, that he has no power over anything, so He said (exalted is He), bringing out the pronoun explicitly with what indicates his contemptibility, to disparage his matter and to repel people from him: ﴿And Satan promises them only﴾, i.e., the one who is burned, the one cast out under the curse: of there being no resurrection, of long life, of the intercession of the gods, and the like. ﴿Nothing but delusion﴾. And "al-ghurur" (delusion) is the decoration of error with what makes it appear to be right.

Then he returned to confronting him with what belittles his affair, for confronting with belittlement is more wounding. He stated plainly the outcome of that, which is that he is unable to do anything except by His permission, glory be to Him, and that he is prevented from whatever He has not decreed for him, in order to repel what might be suggested by what preceded (p-471) that he has independent influence over anything. So He said (Exalted is He): ﴿Indeed﴾; that is: exert your utmost effort, for I have empowered you over the people of desires as an increase in your wretchedness, by what I willed concerning them before creating you and them. You cannot transgress any part of it to My sincere servants, and to those whom I have chosen for My worship. Indeed ﴿My servants﴾, whom I have qualified for being attributed to Me, and who have upheld the true right of servanthood to Me through piety and goodness, ﴿you have no authority over them﴾; that is: in any manner whatsoever; ﴿over them﴾; that is: you cannot mislead them or lead them into a sin that is not forgiven, for I have granted them success in relying upon Me, so I have sufficed them against your affair. ﴿And sufficient is your Lord﴾; that is: the One who brought you into being, the One who manages your affair, ﴿as a Disposer of affairs﴾; who preserves what He is entrusted with from everything that could corrupt it.

When He had mentioned that He is the Guardian (al-Wakil), the One for whom no other is sufficient in protecting, due to His exclusive comprehensive knowledge and perfect power, He followed this with some of His acts that point to that. So He said (Exalted is He), returning to the proofs of tawhid (divine oneness), which is the greatest aim, through the circumstances of the sea in which they are sincere (yakhlusuna) in the style of direct address, seeking to win them over to repentance: ﴿Your Lord﴾, i.e., the One who is good to you, is the one ﴿who drives﴾, i.e., who propels, pushes, and facilitates, ﴿for you﴾, i.e., for your benefit, ﴿the ships﴾ in which He carried you along with your father Noah (peace be upon him), ﴿upon the sea so that you may seek﴾, i.e., that you may strive earnestly to seek through it kinds of benefit that are difficult or hard to reach on land, ﴿of His bounty﴾. Then He gave the reason for this act of His with His saying (Exalted is He): ﴿Indeed, He is﴾, i.e., He did that for you, because He ﴿has been﴾, i.e., eternally and everlastingly, ﴿to you﴾, i.e., O believers specifically, ﴿Merciful﴾, i.e., bestowing honor by granting success in doing what pleases Him, in trade and otherwise, and not for any reason other than that. Or this may be an address to the whole of mankind, in which case the meaning is: He singled you out with this from among the animals.

When the intended audience was specifically the believers, even though the address was to the whole group, He singled out the polytheists in the same way and said: ﴿And when﴾, that is, when He bestows upon you all kinds of good and you ascribe partners to Him, glory be to Him, and when ﴿harm touches you﴾. He did not say "when I touch you [with harm]," attributing it to Himself. This is to teach us good manners in addressing Him: we attribute good to Him but not evil, although we believe that all of it is His act. It also alerts us that evil is something one should disavow and keep away from. ﴿Harm in the sea﴾, from the surging of the water and its turbulence due to the raging of the wind and the swelling of the waves, ﴿goes astray﴾, that is, it departs and vanishes from your remembrance and your thoughts, ﴿those you call upon﴾ from among all existing things, ﴿except Him﴾ alone. So you sincerely direct your supplication to Him, knowing that nothing else will save you. ﴿Then when He delivers you﴾ from drowning and brings you gradually ﴿to the land, you turn away﴾ from sincerity towards Him and return to associating partners with Him. ﴿And man is ever ungrateful﴾, that is, this kind [of creature]; ﴿ungrateful﴾ means extremely concealing of what ought to be made manifest. The word "man" (al-insan) is stated explicitly in a place where a pronoun (idmar) would normally be expected, to alert that this attribute does not belong only to them but applies to this whole species, because of its natural disposition toward deficiencies, except for the one whom Allah has made sincere to Himself.

(p-473) Since the sense is: "You turned away after He had delivered you, and thereby you disbelieved; and disbelief is a quality that clings to you. As a consequence of that, you feel secure, meaning you act with the conduct of one who feels secure"—He rebuked them for this matter, because it is among the most extreme of ignorance. So He (Exalted) said: ﴿Do you feel secure﴾; that is, have you been saved from the sea, so that you feel secure after coming out of it, ﴿that He will cause the earth to swallow you﴾ (an-nakhsifa); that is, by what He possesses of majesty, ﴿on the side of the land﴾. It indicates the intensity of their haste into disbelief upon reaching the first shore by His saying (Exalted): ﴿on the side of the land﴾; that is, He will cause you to vanish into it, on whatever side of it you may be, because His power to make you vanish into the dust on all sides is the same as His power to make you vanish into the water. Therefore the intelligent person should let his fear of Allah be equal on all sides. ﴿Or﴾ do you feel secure, if your hearts have grown too hard to reflect on the like of this, that He will ﴿send against you﴾ (an-nursila 'alaykum), from above, some of His command, ﴿a sandstorm (hasiban)﴾; that is, one that pelts with pebbles (al-hasba'), that is, small stones; so said al-Razi in al-Lawami'. Al-Rummani said: "Stones with which one is pelted"; it is said "yuhsabu bihi" when one is struck by it, pelted repeatedly. End of quotation.

That storm pelts you in your faces, or over your heads, with a pelting that destroys the like of it, as happened to the people of Lot. ﴿Indeed We sent against them a sandstorm﴾. It is also said that "al-hasib" is the wind; and it was not said "hasibah," because it is an attribute that is inherent to it, and it has no masculine form to which it shifts in some state; so it is like "ha'id" (menstruating). ﴿Then you will not find﴾, O people, ﴿for yourselves﴾, and it is unrestricted so as to be general, ﴿any guardian (wakilan)﴾ who will save you from that, nor from anything else, just as you did not find in the sea any guardian other than Him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 69:

﴿Do you feel secure﴾; if stupidity has exceeded its limit with you, and you do not allow that; ﴿that He will return you to it﴾; i.e., to the sea, by what We have of greatness, which compels you to that and makes you acquiesce to it, even if you dislike it; ﴿another time﴾; through causes that compel you to that; ﴿and send against you﴾; i.e., by what We have of the attribute of majesty; ﴿a violent storm﴾; and it is the one that breaks with intensity; ﴿of wind﴾; as you are accustomed to its like, O you whose thoughts have stopped at sensible things, so that they have consented thereby to be like beasts, understanding only particulars that are observed; ﴿and drown you﴾; i.e., in the sea, in which We placed you for Our greatness; ﴿for what you disbelieved﴾; as one of you does when he gains power over someone who has denied his kindness; ﴿then you will not find for yourselves﴾; even if you go to great lengths in seeking, and your times are prolonged in perfecting the means; and since the unrestricted negation at the end of the preceding verse, although it intends generality, may be claimed to be restricted by something that contradicts the intended meaning, and since the aim here is to frighten with His might, may He be glorified, sometimes by causing the earth to swallow, and sometimes by other means, He restricted it by what specifies the intended meaning, and He placed His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿against Us﴾ first, as an indication of the dazzling greatness; ﴿in respect of it﴾; i.e., in respect of what We did to you; ﴿a pursuer﴾; i.e., one who pursues Us on account of it.

In the course of establishing, through these clauses, what He had made easy for them of the land and eased for them of the perils of the sea, within a context of warning, He followed it with the statement that He did this to honour them above the rest of His creatures. This is consistent with His power over what He wills, in the differentiation among things that were equal at the time of their first creation. The purpose is that they may infer from this the ease of the resurrection (al-i'adah). This points to the fact that He composed the essence of the human being from a soul (nafs) that is the noblest of souls, by which He preferred it over the vegetative faculties (al-quwa al-nabatiyyah, the faculties of plant life) of nourishment (al-ightidha'), growth (al-numuww), and reproduction (al-tawlid), through sense perception (al-hiss), outwardly and inwardly, and through voluntary motion (al-harakah bil-ikhtiyar). He singled it out, above all animals, with the rational faculty (al-quwwah al-'aqilah), which apprehends the realities of things as they are, through which the light of knowledge of God (ma'rifat Allah) is made manifest, in which the radiance of His majesty (kibriya') shines, which looks out upon the two worlds of creation and command, and which encompasses the categories of created beings, spirits and bodies, as they are. Thus the human soul became the noblest of the souls of this world, and likewise the human body, by its distinction in upright stature (i'tidal al-qamah), its extension, its use of the hand, and other things. Then He said, exalted is He, connecting it to what the context guides toward (such as saying: "We have honoured you thereby, through the driving of the ship and your deliverance in times of hardship"), or to: "And We have certainly preferred...":

﴿And We have certainly honoured the children of Adam﴾; that is, by Our greatness, with a great honour; ﴿the children of Adam﴾; that is, above all clay (al-tin), through growth, and above all that grows by life, and above all animals through speech. The deletion of the object of the honouring indicates its generality over all creation. All of this is a measure of the power to resurrect. ﴿And We carried them on the land﴾, upon beasts and other things; ﴿and on the sea﴾, upon ships and other things; ﴿and We provided them with good things﴾; that is, a provision befitting Our greatness; ﴿of the good things﴾; that is, the most delightful of fruits and sustenance, which other animals eat only as chaff; ﴿and We preferred them﴾ in their persons, through the excellence of their form, and in their attributes, through knowledge that produces the happiness of both abodes, and in Our provision for them as previously mentioned.

Since He deleted the object of the honouring to indicate generality, and since most of its members are astray, He said for this reason: ﴿above many of those We have created﴾; that is, by Our greatness with which We created them. He emphasised the verb with the verbal noun, indicating their thorough excellence in virtue, and so He said, exalted is He: ﴿with decided preference﴾. This is the case for the collective; as for the sincere devotees (al-khullas), they are the most excellent of creation, because of what we know of their treatment of themselves through sincerity (al-ikhlas) and their striving against their desires, given the defects with which their souls are naturally imprinted and the subtle corruptions they contain, until they mounted, after the rank of faith (iman), the two degrees of taqwa (God-consciousness) and ihsan (excellence). The placing of the command to the angels to prostrate to Adam, peace be upon him, as a preparation for this verse, is the strongest proof of this.

When He, glory be to Him, had established His power over preference in sensory and spiritual life, and over distinguishing between things in the two (matters), thereby establishing His power over resurrection, and concluded this by the preferring of the children of Adam, and the Day of Religion being the greatest day on which preference becomes manifest, He substituted for His saying, ﴿the day He calls you﴾, while warning against His overpowering acts on that day and encouraging the acquisition of virtues in this day, His saying, exalted is He: ﴿The day We shall call﴾; that is, with that greatness; ﴿every people﴾; that is, of you; ﴿with their leader﴾; that is, with the one they followed, whom they obeyed. It will be said: "O followers of Noah! O followers of Abraham! O followers of Jesus! O followers of Muhammad!" Then they will stand, and their righteous will be distinguished from their deviant. And it will be said: "O followers of desire! O followers of the Fire! O followers of the sun! O followers of the idols!" and the like of this. Or the meaning is that they are bound by their deeds to which We tied them, as the bond of a follower to his leader, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And every human being We have fastened his omen to his neck﴾ [al-Isra: 13]. He called them "leader" because they took them as their aim and strove to reach them. And We will hand to them the books in which Our recording angels have counted those deeds (p-478). ﴿Whoever is given his book in his right hand﴾; from among them, from whoever is given anything; ﴿his book in his right hand﴾; these are the ones with insight of heart, due to their piety and their goodness; and they are the ones with insight in this world, and whoever was insightful in this world will be more insightful in the Hereafter, and more rightly guided in the way. ﴿Those﴾; that is, those of high rank; ﴿will read their book﴾; that is, they will renew its reading and repeat it, out of joy at what is in it, as is the custom of everyone who is delighted by a book; ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾ by any reduction of a good deed at all, by any wrongdoer at all; ﴿a thread﴾; that is, anything that is at the extreme of paucity and insignificance. Rather, they will be increased according to the sincerity of their intentions, the purity of their characters, and the purification of their deeds. As for whoever is given his book in his left hand, he will not read his book, because he was blind in this abode.

﴿And whoever is﴾ [among them] ﴿in this﴾ [world], ﴿blind﴾, that is, astray, who acts in matters the way a blind person acts in taking up things, not guided to take what benefits him and leave what harms him, and not distinguishing between good and evil; ﴿then he in the Hereafter﴾, because everyone is raised upon what he died upon, ﴿will be blind﴾, that is, more blind than he was in this world, whose aim does not succeed, who is not guided to what is right, and who is unable to read a book, because of what it contains of things that necessitate punishment. He did not say "ashaddu 'aman" (more blind), as people say of the attributes that are fixed in one state, such as squinting, redness, blackness and the like, because this is meant as blindness of the heart, which by its nature increases and occurs at every moment, one thing after another, so it differs from what does not increase. Abu 'Amr did not pronounce it with imala (vocalic inclination, a recitation feature) even though the first was pronounced with imala, to show that its meaning is "af'alu min kadha" (a comparative form), so it is intermediate, and imala is only good at the ends of words. And because this is its meaning, He linked to it His saying (exalted is He): ﴿and more astray in way﴾, because this world is the world of acquisition and of ascent by means, whereas that one has nothing of that. Thus the verse is of al-ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which two parts are mentioned and each omits what corresponds to the other): it affirmed the giving of the record in the right hand and the reading first, as evidence for the omission of their opposites second; and it affirmed blindness second, as evidence for the omission of its opposite first.

(p-479)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 73:

When he had established that whoever abandons the path of right guidance is like the blind, and whoever follows it is like the one who sees, he followed this with its proof. So he said, warning those who see against being deceived by the whisperings of the wretched: ﴿And if﴾; that is, and most of these are blind, having been tempted within themselves by their desires, despite Our clarifying the path of right guidance through this wisdom which We revealed to you, until it became clearer than the sun. ﴿And indeed the enemies﴾ ﴿almost﴾; that is, they came close, in this worldly life, because of their blindness within themselves to the protection of Allah for you, through their blindness to what you were created with of intelligence, goodness of nature, keenness of disposition, penetrating understanding, and the far reach of insight in discerning the deceptions of deceivers and the schemes of schemers. (p. 480) This is because the subtleties become manifest in the polished mirror of your heart and the transparent clarity of your thought. Since "in" (إنْ) was a lightened form of the heavy (إنَّ), he brought the distinguishing lam (اللّام الفارقة) between it and the negating particle. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿they would surely tempt you﴾; that is, they would mix with you in a manner of gaining control, directing you toward their aim, through their great deceit, by enticing you to conform to what they know of the outward of the worldly life. ﴿away from that which We have revealed﴾; that is, by what We possess of greatness; ﴿to you﴾; of wisdom; ﴿so that you would fabricate﴾; that is, you would deliberately invent; ﴿against Us﴾; against Our greatness; ﴿other than it﴾; such as driving away those to whom We revealed the command to persevere with them, out of their hope of the Islam of one whose conversion would bring about the conversion of a great multitude of them, because of his nobility, and similar things which Allah, exalted is He, intended, and He knows best His intent. Al-Rummani said: The root of fitnah (temptation) is what is sought in order to free a thing from what has entangled it.

﴿And then﴾; that is, had you inclined toward them; ﴿they would have taken you﴾; that is, with the utmost eagerness; ﴿as a close friend﴾. Whoever is a close friend of the disbelievers is not a close friend of Allah. But you perceived your right guidance, so you adhered to the command of Allah, while they remained in their blindness, completing Our preference of you over every creature.

It has already been mentioned shortly before what the root "fa-ra" revolves around, namely expansiveness. There remain from its inverted forms the ya'i (middle-weak) and the hamzated forms. So the meaning of "faraytu al-adim" (I split the hide) is: I cut it, whether badly or properly, because it thereby becomes wider. (p. 481) Al-Qazzaz said: "al-Fary" is the verbal noun of "faraytu al-adim" when you split it for repair, and "afraytuhu" when you split it for corruption; as if its hamza is for removal. Abu 'Ubayda related: "faraytu al-shay'" and "afraytuhu" mean I cut it; and "fara al-kadhib" and "iftarahu" mean he invented it, because it is an expansion of speech and an addition beyond what truthfulness requires, and a transgression of the limit. "Fara al-mazadah" means he sewed it and made it; al-Qazzaz said: he stitched it, because it holds what it could not hold before stitching. He said: The root of "al-fary" is splitting, meaning that stitching occurs in the split; so the relation is by locus. "Fara al-ard" means he traversed and crossed it, likening it to a hide. "Fariya," like "radiya," means he was bewildered and astonished, from naming by the cause, because the cause of astonishment is a multitude and greatness in what is perceived. "Afraha" means he corrected it, or ordered its correction, because correction is expansion relative to corruption. "Afra fulanan" means he blamed him, because it entails an increase in speech by which the one blamed argues. "Al-Firyah" means clamor, because it is an excess beyond ordinary speech; with a kasra it means lying; and like "ghaniyy," it means a fabricated, manufactured matter, or a great one; and a wide bucket is likewise called "firyah." Milk at the moment it is milked, due to the rising of foam, is also so called. "Tafarra al-shay'" means it split; "al-'ayn" means it gushed forth; and "huwa yafri al-fariyy" (he brings the marvelous in his work), like "ghaniyy": (p. 482) he produces the wonderful in his action.

Al-Qazzaz said: "taraktu fulanan yafri wa yaqudd" means I left so-and-so cutting and slashing, that is, sharp in the matter; and "fulanun yafri mundhu al-yawm" means he has come with something marvelous, because only what exceeds sufficiency amazes.

"Al-Rufah" is chaff, because it is what remains beyond the grain. "Al-Rufah" is also a small creature that hunts, called "anaq al-ard" (the female ostrich of the earth), because its condition is wider than that of what does not hunt. This was mentioned by the author of Mukhtasar al-'Ayn under the weak-ya' root, so its pattern is "thubah." The author of al-Qamus mentioned it under the ha', and said regarding its referent, which is chaff, that it is like "suradd"; then he mentioned it under the weak-waw in "w-r-f," and said: "al-Rufah," like "thubah," is chaff. So his statement was inconsistent, and therefore the Mukhtasar al-'Ayn must be accepted. But the Imam Abu Ghalib ibn al-Tayyani, to whom one submits, mentioned it in his book al-Mu'abb under the inverted "r-h-f," and said, attributing it to the Kitab al-'Ayn, the following text: "al-Rufah" is chaff. Another said: it is said in a proverb: "The tuffah has become independent of the ruffah." And "al-Tuffah" is the anaq al-ard, a creature like the fox, malicious, which hunts every thing, because it eats (p. 483) only meat. Abu Hanifa said the same. All of that ended, word for word. Al-Qamus said in the weak-letter section: "al-Tuffah" is mentioned under "t-f-f." He said under the ha': "al-Tuffah," like "thubbah," is the anaq al-ard. He said under the fa': "al-Tuffah," like "qufffah," is a creature like a dog's pup or like a mouse. And "istaghnat al-tuffah 'an al-ruffah" (the tuffah has become independent of the ruffah), and both may be pronounced with lightening; it is struck for a base person when he is satiated. So perhaps this difference is due to dialects, and Allah knows best.

In Mukhtasar al-'Ayn: "al-Urfi," like "kurkiyy," is pure, good milk, because of its abundance, like what is deep within; the Mukhtasar made it ya'i, while al-Qamus made it waw-based, then he repeated it in the hamzated section and said: "al-Urfi," like "qumriyy," is pure milk. Al-Qazzaz in the ya'i section cited: "rafaytu al-rajul urafihi murafatan," meaning I agreed with him, because that is more expansive in companionship. "Al-Rif," with a kasra, is fertility. Al-Qamus said: "a land in which there is crops and fertility, and abundance of food and drink, and what is near water in the land of the Arabs, or where there are greenery, waters, and crops." "Rafa al-badawi" means he came to the rif. "Al-Raf" is wine, and it exists only from abundance. "Ardun rayyifah," like "kayyisah," means fertile land. "Arafat al-ard" means the land became fertile.

From the hamzated forms: "rafa'a al-safinah," like "manaa," and "arfa'aha" means he brought it near the shore, (p. 484) because of the expansion of those within it on land; and relative to it, it is for negation. The place is "marfa'," and it may be pronounced "marfu'." "Rafa'a baynahum" means he reconciled them; "arfa'a" means he inclined, combed, drew near, approached, favored, and made concessions, and "dara'a" like "raf'a," and he turned to it; "tarafa'u" means they agreed and conspired. "Al-yarfa'i," like "al-yalma'i," is a shepherd of sheep; the fleeing ostrich male; the gazelle that is swift in fleeing and turns away; and one whose heart is torn from terror, as if likened to the male ostrich in the expansiveness of its movement and its lack of steadiness; this also resembles the boiling of a pot in exceeding its limit. "Raffa'tu al-'arus tarfi'atan wa tarfi'an" was already mentioned under the waw-based forms. "Al-Ra'f" is wine; also the compassionate man, or "al-ra'fah" is the most intense mercy or the gentlest of it. There is no doubt that this enters into expansiveness. "Ra'f" is a place, or a sandy tract, and perhaps both are wide. "Al-Fara'" like "jabal" and "sahab" is the wild ass, or its young one, because of its great aversion, like a pot in its boiling. "Amrun fariy'" is like "fariyy." "Kullu al-saydi fi jawfi al-fara'" means all of it is less than it. "Fara'" with fatha and damma is an island in Yemen, perhaps because it abounds with them. "Al-Fa'r" is known; its singular is "fa'rah," and its plural is "fi'ran." It was named for its leaping in its running, and because it has more freedom of movement among creatures, walking on walls, ceilings, and the like. "Al-Fa'rah" is also a tree, and the musk pod (p. 485) of musk; al-Qamus said: or the correct approach is to list "fara al-misk" under "f-w-r," because of the spreading of its fragrance; or it may be hamzated, because it is shaped like a mouse. "Fa'ara," like "mana'a," means he dug, hid, and buried; it may be from expansiveness and from its negation. "Laban fa'ir," like "kitf," is milk into which a mouse has fallen. "Ardun fa'irah; wa mafarah" means land abounding in mice. "Afarat al-qidr" (with fatha) "ta'fir af'ran" means its boiling became intense. "Al-insan" means he leapt and ran; "al-ba'ir" means he became lively and fat after exertion, like "afira" (like "fariha") in both; and he was quick in service. The one who runs before a person and serves him is "mi'far." "Al-Ufurrah," with two dammas and the rā' doubled, means a group (which in Mukhtasar al-'Ayn he restricted to "one with clamor"), and calamity, and mixing; all of this is clear in expansiveness and excess beyond sufficiency. "Al-Ufurrah" also means intensity of evil, because of its intense boiling like a pot; and severity of winter, or absolute severity; and "min al-sayf" means its beginning, because it expands by it. Al-Qamus said: its first letter may be pronounced with a fatha, and it may be vocalized in all cases. "Al-Urufah," with a damma, means the boundary between lands, and a knot; this seems to be the removal of expansiveness. "Al-Urfi," like "qumriyy," means the surveyor. "Urrifa 'ala al-ard ta'rifan" means boundaries were set for it and it was divided. (p. 486) "Ta'rif al-habl" means tying its knot. "Huwa mu'arifi" means its boundary is to my boundary, in dwelling and place. And Allah is the Granter of success.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 74:

When Allah—glorified is He—mentioned what was in that of his right guidance (ﷺ), He followed it with an explanation that it was only by Allah's protection (ʿiṣmah) for him, so that he would increase in gratitude.
