So He—exalted is He—said: ﴿And had We not made you firm﴾; that is, by what We have of greatness, in accordance with what We had commanded, because of what preceded: that We are with those who have taqwa and those who are doers of good; and you are the foremost of the God-fearing and the good-doers. ﴿You would almost have inclined toward them﴾; that is, you would have come close to it—toward the enemies—﴿a little﴾; because of your love for their guidance and your eagerness for their benefit. But We had protected you, so you did not incline toward them at all, neither a little nor a lot, and you did not even come close to it, as the particle "law-lā" indicates, because it enters upon a nominal sentence and then a verbal sentence, to link the non-occurrence of the second to the occurrence of the first. So the non-occurrence of coming close to inclining is linked to the occurrence of firmness. This is because "law-lā" indicates the absence of the second due to the absence of the first; and here it enters upon "lā," the negating particle, so it indicates the absence of coming close to inclining due to the absence of the negation of firmness; and the absence of a negation is an existence. So firmness exists, and coming close to inclining is absent. It is also permissible that the intended meaning is to show the intensity of their deceit and the extent of their trickery to a degree whose description cannot be grasped. In that case the verb is attributed to him (ﷺ), while what is intended is its attribution to them, so that the meaning is: they nearly made you come close to inclining toward them, just as you say to your companion, "You nearly killed yourself," meaning: you did an act by which you came close to someone else killing you because of your action. This verse is among the clear proofs of the virtues particular to the Prophet (ﷺ) in the nobility of his essence, the purity of his origin, the excellence of his intellect, and the goodness of his lineage; for it shows that if he had been left to himself, and to what Allah had created in his nature and disposition of the complete qualities and virtuous attributes, and had Allah not supported him, during prophethood, with the firmness He granted him beyond that, he would not have inclined toward them—though they were the most acute of people in thought, the purest in understanding, the most knowledgeable of deception, and of great number, great patience, and great endurance—with any inclination at all, in principle; and their utmost was only to bring him close to inclining a little. Glorified is He who singles out whom He wills with what He wills, and He is the Possessor of great bounty.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 75:

﴿Then﴾; i.e., if you had come close to inclining toward them as described; ﴿We would have made you taste﴾; i.e., with Our greatness; ﴿double the punishment﴾; of; ﴿life and double the punishment﴾; of; ﴿death﴾; i.e., that punishment doubled.

This root revolves around weakness (al-wahy); it necessarily entails strengthening by doubling, with a kasra on the ḍād (ḍiʿf), i.e., the equivalent and what exceeds it; and everything that has a multiple is weak without it. (p-488) The doubling (ḍiʿf), which is an equivalent added to its equal, necessarily entails strength. From weakness (al-wahy) come: "ḍaʿf" and "ḍuʿf," with a fatḥa and with a ḍammah, which is the opposite of strength. It is said: "ḍaʿf" with a fatḥa refers to the intellect and opinion, and with a ḍammah to the body. "Ḍaʿīf" means blind (Ḥimyarite usage). "Arḍun muḍʿafa" (passive form) means: a weak rain has struck it. "Ḍiʿf al-shayʾ" with a kasra means its equivalent, because everything that has an equivalent is weak. "Ḍiʿfāhu" means its two equivalents. It is said: "laka ḍiʿfuhu," i.e., its two equivalents and three times its equivalents, because the origin of doubling is an unlimited increase. "Ḍāʿaftu al-shayʾ" means: I added two things to the thing so that it became three. "Aḍʿāf al-kitāb" means: the spaces between its lines, because they are equivalents to the lines in whiteness and an addition to them. From the strength that necessarily accompanies the equivalent: "aḍʿāf al-badan" means its limbs, because most of them are in pairs; or it means its bones, because they are the strongest part of it. Also from weakness, in inverted form, is "ḍafaʿa," which means to pass wind and break wind; likewise the inverted form "faḍaʿ." "Al-ḍafʿ" is the dung of the elephant. "Al-ḍafʿānah" is the fruit of the saʿdānah plant, which has thorns, is round, as if it were a disc. So the meaning, and God knows best, is: We would have made you taste the weakness of life and the weakness of death, multiplied many times over.

Since strength after this is at the furthest extreme, He expressed it with the particle of delay in His saying (Exalted is He): ﴿then you would not find for yourself﴾; i.e., even if you were the greatest of creation and the highest in resolve; (p-489) ﴿against Us any helper﴾. The verse indicates that the ugliness of a wrong is magnified in proportion to the great standing of its perpetrator and the height of his rank; and that the slightest flattery of the deceivers is opposition to God and departure from His guardianship. So whoever recites it should reflect upon it, feel the fear of God, and grasp the great firmness required in religion.

When he had explained that they tried to win him over with gentleness, to the point that they nearly swayed him had it not been for divine protection ('ismah, safeguarding from error), this indicates that they then frightened him, to the point that they nearly drove him out of his homeland before the specific permission to emigrate (hijrah). So He, exalted, said: ﴿And indeed﴾; that is, indeed they ﴿nearly﴾; that is, the enemies ﴿would have driven you out﴾ (ليستفزونك, layastafizzunaka); that is, they would have unsettled you (yastakhiffunaka) through great harm, as is customary in such matters, ﴿from the land﴾; that is, Makkah, which is in fact the whole land, because it is its mother, ﴿in order to expel you from it﴾, even though your presence among them is a mercy to them, so none is more blind than they. The root of "fazz" (الفزّ) is cutting with force, as said by al-Rummani (الرُّمّانِيُّ). ﴿And then﴾; that is, if they had expelled you; ﴿they would not remain after you﴾ (لا يلبثون خلافك); that is, after your expulsion, had they expelled you; ﴿except for a little﴾. And they will know, when We permit you to depart, how We shall pour down punishment upon them, a short time after your departure, with your long spear, your polished sword, and the swords of your believing followers, for the establishment of this religion. Allah, glory be to Him, fulfilled this threat by slaying their chieftains at the Battle of Badr (غزوة بدر), in Ramadan, in the second year after the hijrah, eighteen months after his emigration (ﷺ). He also forbade the polytheists who had expelled him (ﷺ) from sacred Makkah the entry into it and residence in its sanctuary (حريمها) from the Arabian Peninsula, honoring him (ﷺ) and taking vengeance upon whoever holds any part of the disbelief of those who expelled him.

He put ﴿يلبثون﴾ (yalbathuna) in the nominative, because ﴿إذًا﴾ (idhan), when it comes after a waw or a fa', may be cancelled (ilgha', الإلغاء) in grammar, since it is then in the middle of the sentence, just as it must be cancelled at the end of a sentence.

In the verse there is a demonstration that the ignorant person does not cease to set snares for the scholar and to seek out calamities for him, and that this returns upon him as ruin, both in the present and in the end.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 77:

When He informed him of that, He made him know that it is His way (sunnah) with all the Messengers. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The way (sunnata)﴾; that is, "like the way (ka-sunnati)"; or "Our way with you is the way of ﴿those whom We sent﴾"; that is, with the greatness that We possess.

Since sending (al-irsal) had its blessing spread across all times through this greatness, together with what surrounded it of upright natural disposition (qawim al-fitrah), He dropped the preposition and said, exalted is He: ﴿before you﴾; that is, in all the past times; ﴿of Our messengers﴾; by making their existence among their peoples a mercy to their peoples. Then, if the peoples expelled them, We hastened punishment upon whoever approved of their expulsion (p-491) ﴿and you will not find any alteration in Our way﴾; that is, in respect of the greatness it possesses; ﴿alteration﴾; that is, by any other changer who could alter it. However, this community was singled out from the earlier nations in that they will not be punished with the punishment of total annihilation (al-isti'sal), in honour of them through this noble Prophet.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 78:

When he (ﷺ) had established the matter of the foundations of the religion, namely divine oneness (tawhid) and the power to resurrect (al-ma'ad, the Return), and had established their matter in the best manner, and had won them over with His blessings and warned them of His punishments, and had established that He, glory be to Him, had protected him (peace be upon him) from their trial through prosperity and adversity, by what He had illuminated him with of insight (basirah) and had perfected in his outward and inward states, it became known that he had devoted himself to worship and prepared himself for vigilance (muraqabah) before God. So He began with its most noble part, and thereby connected to it His saying (exalted is He): ﴿Establish﴾, that is, truly in deed, and figuratively through the resolve to do it, ﴿the prayer﴾, by performing all its conditions, its pillars, its beginnings and its ends, such that it becomes as though it stands by itself. For it is the core of worship, with what it contains of pure intimate communion with God, by turning away from everything other than Him, and the annihilation of everything ("other than Him"), by what shines forth of the lights of the Divine Presence, before which every perishable thing dissolves. In this there is a great indication that prayer is the greatest helper against enemies, who intend by their deceit to provoke the friends of God, and the most effective of things in repelling adversity and the most attracting of every prosperity. For this reason, "the Prophet (ﷺ), when a matter distressed him, would have recourse to prayer," as has been previously cited at the end of surah al-Hijr. Then He specified for him the times by His saying (exalted is He): (p-492) ﴿at the decline of the sun﴾, that is, its passing of the meridian, its yellowing, and its setting. Al-Fayruzabadi said in al-Qamus: "dalakat al-shams" means it set, or it yellowed, or it inclined, or it passed the meridian from the middle of the sky. Thus in this word there is an indication of the Zuhr (noon prayer), the 'Asr (afternoon prayer), and the Maghrib (sunset prayer), through the use of the homonym (mushtarak, a word having several meanings) in its meanings. As for Zuhr and Maghrib, it is clear; and as for 'Asr, it is because the beginning of its time is the beginning of the sun's yellowing. The clearest proof of this is that He made the establishment (of prayer) extend to the time of 'Isha', saying (exalted is He): ﴿until﴾, urging the intention that one should pray whenever the time comes, so that one would be constantly in prayer, for a person who is awaiting prayer is in prayer. Thus it explains that the time of Maghrib runs from the decline, which is the setting, until the shafaq (twilight) disappears, ﴿the darkness of the night﴾. Al-ghasaq is the darkness of the beginning of the night, and it is the time of sleep. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': it is the intensification of the darkness of the night. Al-Rummani said: its darkness appearing. Then He joined to it, by changing the context, His saying (exalted is He): ﴿and the recitation of dawn﴾, as though He said: then sleep, and establish the recitation of the dawn. ﴿Of dawn﴾ is an indication of the morning. It was said that it is in the accusative as an incitement (ighra'). It seems He referred to it by the Qur'an because, although it is the greatest pillar of prayer, the recitation in it is lengthened more than in other prayers, and it is recited aloud in it, unlike its counterpart, the 'Asr; and (He used this expression) as an enticement toward it, because of the heaviness of waking from sleep.

Since rising from sleep is difficult, He gave a reason in order to encourage, using an explicit noun rather than a pronoun (p-493), because the context is one of exaltation. So He said (exalted is He): ﴿Indeed, the recitation of dawn was ever witnessed﴾. It is witnessed by two groups of angels, and it is worthy that everyone should witness it, because of the delight it has for hearing, the gladdening of the heart, and the revival of the spirit. Thus the verse came to encompass the prayers (all of them). Al-Bukhari narrated in the Book of Tafsir, from Abu Hurayrah (may God be pleased with him), who said: "The merit of praying in congregation over praying alone is twenty-five degrees; and the angels of the night and the angels of the day gather at the Fajr prayer." Abu Hurayrah said: "Recite, if you wish: ﴿Indeed, the recitation of dawn﴾," to the end of the verse. They said: this is evidence for the obligation of praying at the beginning of the time, and that praying Fajr in the darkness (taghlis) before dawn is more excellent.

Then, after this, He urged him to tahajjud (voluntary night prayer), because of its excellence and its greater weight. So He said, may He be exalted: ﴿And from﴾; that is, "and devote to it a portion of" or "stand in prayer for part of" ﴿the night, and perform tahajjud with it﴾; that is, abandon sleep (al-huju'ud, which is sleep) for prayer; ﴿with it﴾; that is, with the Qur'an in general, so this is a good instance of istikhdam (a rhetorical device in which one term is used in one sense and a pronoun referring back to it in another); ﴿as a supererogatory act (nafilah) for you﴾; that is, an addition specific to you. 'Abd al-Ghafir al-Farisi said in Majma' al-Gharib: The root of "nafl" is increase, and from it comes "al-anfal" (the spoils), the surplus over the booty which Allah made lawful for this community. Abu 'Abd Allah al-Qazzaz said: "al-nawafil" are bounties. From this they say: "So-and-so is one from whom bounties are hoped for." End of quote. So it is an increase for the Prophet (ﷺ) in what is obligatory, and for the community in what is voluntary. It was singled out for him as an encouragement to the community, because they know that he is only singled out for the best of good. It is the time in which the answering of supplication is alluded to by descent to the lowest heaven, which entails nearness, as stated in the sound hadiths that it occurs in the depth of the night. This is because it is the custom of kings in this world to open the door, to draw near to it, to raise the curtain, and to descend from the place of majesty as a sign of granting needs. Anything that is described of Allah, exalted is He, which must be declared free of its apparent meaning, is a metaphor (kinayah) for its necessary implication. A hadith we narrated in the Juz' of al-'Absi confirms this: "On the authority of 'Uthman ibn Abi al-'As, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Indeed, in the night there is an hour in which the gates of heaven are opened, and a caller calls: Is there any supplicant who will be answered?...'" to its end. So this is a great witness to this interpretation.

When He commanded him to tahajjud and humble devotion, and the context was one of greatness, hoping for a gift consistent with the context, He said, may He be exalted: ﴿It may be that﴾; that is, so that you stand in the position of one who hopes that ﴿He will raise you﴾. Since the context had turned to hope, He expressed it with the attribute of benevolence, saying, may He be exalted: ﴿your Lord﴾; that is, the One who bestows favour upon you, after the greater death and before it, just as He raised your soul from the lesser death to His service; ﴿to a station﴾, put in the adverbial sense; ﴿praiseworthy﴾. This is because "'asa" (it may be) indicates hope in what is loved and apprehension in what is disliked; this may weaken, so that doubt arises regarding the matter, and it may strengthen, so that certainty results; here it is for certainty. They said: "'Asa" conveys encouragement of expectation, and whoever raises someone's hopes in something and then denies him it would be shamed, and Allah, exalted is He, is too generous to do that. He expressed it with this word rather than with something indicating certainty, because that is more fitting in the speech of kings, as it is more indicative of majesty. In al-Bukhari's Tafsir, on the authority of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, he said: On the Day of Resurrection people will become kneeling (juthan), every community following its prophet, saying: "O so-and-so, intercede! O so-and-so, intercede!" until intercession reaches the Prophet (ﷺ). That is the day on which Allah raises him to the praiseworthy station.

That is: thus there will appear what he has of his share of his names "Ahmad" and "Muhammad" at that time, through the praise of every living creature, by conveying benefit to each of them in deed, and he has (this) in the commentary and elsewhere, on the authority of Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, may Allah be pleased with them both, that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Whoever says when he hears the call to prayer: 'O Allah, Lord of this perfect call and established prayer, grant Muhammad the wasilah (intercessory station) and the fadilah (excellence), and raise him to the praiseworthy station which You have promised him, my intercession will be lawful for him on the Day of Resurrection.'" He means, and Allah knows best, the special intercession; as for the general intercession, it is for all, without condition.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 80:

When this station was suitable for intercession, and for every station a person stands in, and every station requires success in entering into it and disengaging from it, He followed it (p-496), urging constant watchfulness and a sense of need, with His words, placing the entrance first because it is more important: ﴿And say: My Lord,﴾ that is, O You who brought me into being, who manages my affairs, who is good to me; ﴿cause me to enter,﴾ into every station into which You wish to bring me, sensory and spiritual, worldly and otherworldly; ﴿an entrance of truthfulness,﴾ such that the one who enters it deserves to be told: You are truthful in your word and your deed, for one who has both qualities is not held in high esteem with God. ﴿And cause me to exit,﴾ from everything from which You bring me out; ﴿an exit of truthfulness.﴾

Since truthfulness in affairs may not be accompanied by success, He (Exalted) said: ﴿And grant me,﴾ that is, specifically; ﴿from Yourself,﴾ that is, from Your presence; from the extraordinary things which are the most wondrous of wonders; ﴿an authority,﴾ that is, a proof and might; ﴿to help me.﴾ In this there is an indication of the migration, and that it would be in the manner which time has revealed of greatness, the kind of greatness for which no one has any power (yadan).

When supplication may not be answered, He said, giving him good news that there is nothing between his supplication and its being answered except His saying, and confirming that good news by commanding him to announce it: ﴿Say﴾, i.e., to your allies and your enemies: ﴿The truth has come﴾, and it is everything my Lord commanded me and sent down to me; ﴿and falsehood has vanished﴾, i.e., it was reduced to nothing, nullified, and destroyed; ﴿falsehood﴾, and it is everything that opposes the truth. Then He gave the reason for its vanishing with His saying: ﴿Indeed, falsehood was ever bound to vanish﴾, in itself, by its very nature and disposition, ﴿bound to vanish﴾, a decree God (Exalted is He) decreed from eternity. Al-Bukhari, in his book of Tafsir (exegesis) and elsewhere, related from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him (p-497), who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) entered when there were three hundred and sixty idols around the House, and he began striking them with a stick in his hand, saying: ﴿The truth has come and falsehood has vanished; indeed falsehood was ever bound to vanish﴾ ﴿The truth has come, and falsehood can neither originate nor restore﴾ [Saba': 49]."

The Qur'an, which he (al-Biqa'i) had alluded to in the verse ﴿Establish the prayer﴾, is the greatest cause of the eradication of falsehood, which, like magic, is mere illusion and deception. It also comprises all that has preceded of the divine matters, the Resurrection, and what follows from them. Conjoining it to ﴿And We have honored﴾, He said: ﴿And We send down﴾, meaning, by Our majesty. Then He specified what is sent down by His words, exalted is He: ﴿of the Qur'an﴾, meaning the all-comprehensive, the discriminating, which is the truest of the true, ﴿that which is a healing﴾ for hearts and bodies, ﴿and a mercy﴾, meaning a honor and a strength, ﴿for the believers﴾, meaning those firmly rooted in faith, because it illuminates their hearts from the rust of ignorance and guides them upon the path of right guidance, which is the cause of mercy, and because it protects them from every devil, sickness, and trial, when sincerity is present in seeking healing through it. All of it is thus, and likewise all its parts. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': It is the intimacy of the lovers and the solace of the longing ones, and it is the manifest light, whoever gains insight through it, there is revealed to him of the realities what had been hidden, and there is folded away from him of the calamities what had been spread out, just as falsehood is a disease and a curse for the disbelievers.

﴿And﴾ among the most wondrous of wonders is that this healing ﴿does not increase the wrongdoers﴾, meaning those firmly rooted in this attribute, and they are those who place a thing in other than its place, by turning away from what must be accepted, ﴿except in loss﴾, meaning in deficiency. For when it comes to them and the proof is established against them, they turn away from it, so their turning away becomes an increase in their disbelief, just as the acceptance of the believers of it and their devotion to contemplating it is an increase in their faith.

In al-Darimi, on the authority of Qatada, he said: "No one sat with the Qur'an and then rose from it except with an increase or a decrease." Then he recited this verse.

Then he turned to this understood implication, whose supposition is known, to something more general than it and clearer regarding the trial (fitnah) and audacity (ijtira'); so he (Exalted is He) said: ﴿And when We bestow favor﴾; i.e., by what We possess of greatness; ﴿upon man﴾; i.e., this kind; these people and others; with whatever blessing it may be, from the sending down of the Qur'an and other than it; ﴿he turns away﴾; i.e., from remembrance of the Benefactor; like the aversion of these people at the coming of this blessing, for which there is no blessing like it; ﴿and turns aside﴾; i.e., he moves far away (p-499) in arrogance; ﴿with his side﴾; in insolence and blindness to the realities; ﴿and when evil touches him﴾; i.e., this kind; even if it is little; ﴿he is despairing﴾; i.e., he is extremely hopeless; in panic, and has little trust in what is with him of the mercy of Allah; except for those whom Allah protects and honors by attributing them to Himself; so Satan has no authority over them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 84:

Since the singular noun prefixed with the definite article (al-mufrad al-muhallá bi-l-lam) is generalizing (ya'ummu), this may have prompted some captious objectors to raise an objection, saying: "We see that some people, when they are given something, give thanks, and when they are afflicted, they are patient." This objection is baseless and is not to be heeded. Firstly, because the answer to it has already been given in surah Yunus, peace be upon him, in His saying (Exalted is He): ﴿Thus the deeds of the wasteful have been made attractive to them﴾ [Yunus: 12], that this applies to the wasteful (al-musrifin) and not to others; and by His saying (Exalted is He) in surah Hud, peace be upon him: ﴿except those who are patient﴾ [Hud: 11]. Perhaps He omitted it in this place to indicate that, because their individuals are few, they are as if they were non-existent. Secondly, because the definite noun prefixed with the article (al-muhalla bi-l-lam), whether singular or plural, is equivalent to the particular (al-juz'i), until something arrives that indicates it is universal (kulli). Therefore, (Exalted is He) turned away from it and commanded him to answer both categories, the one alluded to and the one explicitly mentioned. So He (Exalted is He) said: ﴿Say﴾; that is, O the most noble of our creation; ﴿Each﴾ of the grateful and the disbelieving; ﴿acts according to his shakilah﴾ (p-500), that is, his manner which conforms to his spirit and conforms to what We have imprinted upon him of good or evil; ﴿so your Lord﴾; that is, as a consequence, the One who created you and brought you through the stages of growth, and no other, ﴿is most knowing﴾ absolutely ﴿of who is﴾ among you ﴿best guided in way﴾; that is, more rightly guided and more upright in terms of the path, by his piety and his excellence, so that he gives thanks and is patient seeking reward, and He gives him the reward; and of who is ﴿more astray in way﴾, so that punishment befalls him. This is because He knows what He has imprinted upon them in their original creation and what dispositions He has planted in them, whereas others only know people's affairs in their conduct through experience. Imam Ahmad has narrated it, though with a broken chain (munqati'), from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace, said: "If you hear of a mountain that has moved from its place, then believe it; but if you hear of a man who has changed from his character, then do not believe it, for he will return to that for which he was made." All of this concerns actual turning away (al-i'rad bi-l-fi'l); and even if it is potential (bi-l-quwwah), we hold that it is universal (kulliyyah). And Allah knows best about the one who is guided, so that He protects him from turning away and despair, by actuality, with what he has in potentiality.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 85:

When He (glory be to Him) had shown, after expressing wonder at their denial of resurrection, the ignorance of man and the error and forgetfulness he is in, except for the one whom He favored over the offspring of his kind (p-501), just as He favored his clay over the rest of the clay, and concluded with the verse of resemblance (al-mushakalah), of which is the resemblance of some souls to others and their resemblance to natures, and it became clear thereby that He (glory be to Him and exalted) is capable of doing whatever He wills, knowing every thing known, He returned to wondering at them with what pertains to the souls, which by their nature have affinity. So He (exalted) said, connecting it to ﴿And they say: "When we have become bones..."﴾: ﴿And they ask you⦅ about the soul⦆﴾; that is, out of obstinacy and testing; ﴿about the soul⦆﴾, which was previously mentioned that it will be returned to their bodies on the Day of Resurrection, even if they were stones or iron: What is it? Is it a body or not? Is it generated from the mixture of the natures in the body, or is its mixture originated? Is it eternal or created? Since that was obstinacy, while belief in it is not dependent on knowing it, He commanded him to answer them about it with what suits their condition, by His saying (exalted): ﴿Say: "The soul is⦅ of⦆ the command of my Lord"﴾; that is, this is the kind by which bodies become living; ﴿of the command of my Lord﴾; He attributed it to the command, which is the will, although it is among His creation, to honor it, and as an indication that no cause other than Him intervenes between it and His command, but rather He originates it from non-existence. Or it may be said, and this is better: creation is of two kinds: that which is by causation, development and evolution, which is what is rendered in the Qur'an as creation (khalq); and the second is that which is bringing forth from non-existence without causation or evolution, which is expressed as command (amr). Of this is this soul about which they are asked, and every soul in the Qur'an; and likewise what is for preservation and governance, like the angels (al-adyan); and what unites all of this is the sustaining (al-qayyumiyyah), as passed from al-Harrali at the mention of the Holy Spirit in al-Baqarah. This expression therefore conveys that it is originated, that it is not evolved, nor caused, and that it is a subtle body permeating the body, like rosewater in the rose, according to the correct view of the People of the Sunnah. The earlier scholars (al-salaf) refrained from delving deeply into speech about the soul out of courtesy, because they knew that in not answering their question with other than this there is an indication that silence about it is better for them. Then he followed it with an alert to their ignorance, because of their inversion in questions, by their neglect of attending to what they undoubtedly do not comprehend, and what would benefit them in both abodes from this spiritual soul, which is the Qur'an, and their attention to what they do not comprehend of the sensible soul, due to the paucity of their knowledge; and whoever among them understood it does not understand it except with great difficulty. In it there are very many questions for which there is no proof of their answers: among them whether it is spatially bounded or not; whether it is distinct from the self (nafs) or not; and whether it remains after death or not. So we know from it that it is only in general terms, and lack of knowledge of its specific reality does not entail denying it, for most realities of things are unknown, yet they exist.

Thus, "sikanjabin" (a vinegar-based drink): its property is to suppress bile, and the reality of that property is unknown, yet its existence is known; and there is beyond knowledge of what they asked about of the soul, after understanding from it what benefit there is, nothing comparable to that which they abandoned, nor close to it. So He (exalted) said, indicating its origination by its changeability, for it is in the beginning ignorant, then knowledge comes to it little by little (p-503), and everything changeable is originated: ﴿And you have been given⦅ none⦆ of the knowledge﴾ [al-Qasas: 60]; that is, from whichever giver it may be, after you did not know anything; ﴿of knowledge﴾; that is, the absolute of this reality; how then of its difficult aspects? ﴿except a little﴾; and among what you are ignorant of are matters that are necessary for you, because your persistence in ignorance of them is a cause of your destruction in both abodes; so among the most profound ignorance and the most misguided error is that you ask about what the ignorance of it does not harm you, and whose establishment depends on subtle matters and difficult premises, while you leave what ignorance of it harms you in religion and in the worldly life, although it is in utmost clarity, due to the abundance of proofs established upon it, and it has examples before you. And what you asked about is free of deceit and constraint; it alerts you to your frivolity, as a counsel to you, and turns away from answering you about it to what benefits you, out of kindness to you; and for understanding this the earlier scholars kept silent about delving into its matter. The address is to the Jews and the Arabs; as for the Arabs it is clear; and as for the Jews, although they are People of the Book, that is an indication of the vanishing of their knowledge beside the knowledge of God, as will come the indication to it in the saying of al-Khidr to Musa, upon both of them be prayers and peace, concerning the sparrow that pecked from the sea a peck or two; so wherever magnification is ascribed to someone, and its multiplication, it is in relation to other creatures; and wherever its diminishment is mentioned, as in this verse, it is from the standpoint of its attribution to (p-504) the knowledge of God (exalted). And this verse, regarding the occasion of its revelation, has what is thought to be contradictory, for it was narrated in the Sahih from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him) that he was walking with the Prophet (ﷺ) in Madinah, and the Jews asked him about the soul; then revelation came to him; and when the revelation had passed from him, he recited the verse to them."

In al-Sirah al-Hishamiyyah, and al-Dala'il of al-Bayhaqi, and the Tafsir of al-Baghawi, and other tafsirs, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both): "Quraysh sent to the Jews, before the Hijrah, asking them about the Prophet (ﷺ), because they are the first People of the Book and have from the knowledge of the prophets what Quraysh does not have; so they instructed them to ask him about the soul, and about the story of the People of the Cave and Dhu al-Qarnayn. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to them: 'I will inform you of what you asked about tomorrow,' and he did not make an exception; so they departed from him. He remained, as they relate, fifteen nights, with Allah not sending revelation to him concerning that, until the people of Makkah spread rumors about him, and until the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) grieved, and what the people of Makkah were saying was hard upon him." It is also narrated that the delay of the revelation was forty nights, and it is narrated: twelve (p-505) nights. And in the Musnad of Abu Ya'la, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: Quraysh said to the Jews: "Give us something to ask this man about." They said: "Ask him about the soul." So they asked him, and the verse was revealed: ﴿And they ask you⦅ about the soul⦆﴾, the verse. And that and similar narrations, praise be to Allah, are not problematic, for it is to be understood that it was revealed for the first occasion; then when the Prophet (ﷺ) was asked about it a second time, he did not answer with the first answer, either hoping that a clearer one would be given, or fearing that it had been abrogated, or something similar, for a matter he saw; so Allah (glory be to Him) sent it down to him again, as confirmation for him and as informing him that it is the answer. In this there is a sufficient lesson. And in the delay of the answer in this matter is a decisive proof for Quraysh and everyone who has even a little intellect, of the truthfulness of the Prophet (ﷺ) in that this Qur'an is from Allah, which no one other than Him is able to produce; for if he had been able to bring anything of it from his own self, or from anyone among creation, he would have exerted his effort in that, to purify his noble self, his lofty aspiration, and his pure honor, from the like of what they immersed themselves in, due to the breaking of their promise.

And since the soul is of the world of command, which is among the secret of the malakut (the invisible dominion), it was joined to Surat al-Isra', which is among the innermost secrets of the malakut, especially with what he ascended in through the Mi'raj, which was made, because of its strangeness, like a dream (p-506): ﴿And We did not make the vision which We showed you except as a trial for the people﴾ [al-Isra': 60]; and for this reason it was separated from the other two questions, because they are of the world of dominion (mulk). The remainder of the discussion on this will come, God willing (exalted), in Surat al-Kahf.

When he explained their desire for trial (fitnah), by means of changing what was sent down and expelling the Messenger, and what follows from that, until he concluded with their ignorance, since they asked, out of obstinacy, about the sensory spirit, whereas the more beneficial question for them would have been, seeking benefit and understanding, about the fine points of the spirit in its meaning (al-ruh al-ma'nawi), by which God greatly honored them by sending it down to them through a man from among them, the most noble of them in glory, the purest of them in soul, the greatest of them in birth, the most pure in lineage, and the highest of them in resolve, and concluded with the lessening of their knowledge, to indicate that they do not understand except that He (subhanahu) make them understand it, and He is the most knowing of what they understand and what they do not understand, He said, connecting it (ʿatifan) to "and indeed they nearly tempted you" (wa-in kadu la-yaftinunaka), as an admonition to them that if He willed, He would take away, by means of this little knowledge which He granted them, so that ignorance would overwhelm them as they were before, and that the refusal to ask about what concerns them did not suffice them, until they asked about what does not concern them, and desired to replace what benefits them and concerns them with what would destroy and annihilate them, and thus they went astray in word and deed: ﴿And if We willed﴾. Our will is not overpowered by anything. The lam (ل) in "wa-la'in" is the lam of preparation for an oath (lam al-muwatta'ah li-l-qasam), and the answer to the oath is given in place of the answer to the condition, so He said (exalted is He): ﴿We would surely take away﴾ (la-nadhhabanna), i.e., by the greatness that is ours, a taking away that is certain; ﴿that which We have revealed﴾, i.e., by the greatness that is ours, ﴿to you﴾, of what they desired to tempt you with from the Qur'an, since in it is knowledge that would suffice them, were they to turn to understanding it, against anything else, so that no "We" or "Our revelation" would remain with you. And to convey this he did not say "la-adhhabna" (we would take away); ﴿then﴾, i.e., after taking it away, ﴿you would not find for yourself﴾. And since the context here concerns the spirit, which is the revelation, and care for it is greater, he put "bihi" (by it/for it) first. And since the context concerns one who takes what he wills by willing or by compulsion, He said (exalted is He): ﴿against Us﴾, i.e., by the greatness that is ours, which cannot be opposed, ﴿a guardian﴾ who would bring it back to you, or any part of it.

Since there is no refuge from Him, glory be to Him, except in Him, He (Exalted is He) said: ﴿Except﴾; that is, "but you will find" ﴿mercy﴾, initiated and existing ﴿from your Lord﴾; that is, the One who does good to you by bringing you into existence and nurturing you, and who never cuts off His kindness from you at any time; He restores through it [what was lost] to you, and brings you what stands in its place. He expressed the particle of cutting off with the particle of connection, indicating that His mercy, glory be to Him, toward him, which the attribute of His kindness to him necessitates, is—because of its greatness—like a guardian who acts with what is good in every state.

Since, in His sending down the Qur'an to him and then keeping it with him, there is a blessing upon him and upon his community that cannot be counted, He drew attention to this by His saying (Exalted is He), resuming and emphasizing, because the existence of mercy in this manner is among the most astonishing of strange things; it is such that it hardly could be believed, and it is something one delights in mentioning: ﴿Indeed, His grace has always been﴾; that is, a constant state; ﴿upon you﴾; that is, specifically; ﴿great﴾; that is, of utmost greatness. It has been reported that the Qur'an will be taken away at the end of time, by night, from what is in the mushafs and from what is in hearts; and this verse has conveyed that, because the speech of kings conveys the essence of a matter even when it is in the context of a conditional.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 88:

When it was likely that they would say: "If he has missed anything of it, then let him bring the like of it from his own self; and [it is] from what he has acquired from the fables (asatir)," He commanded him to answer them concerning this with his saying, indicating the content of what came before it: ﴿Say﴾. And since what is intended here is the equivalence in every detail with all the surahs, in true meanings and in fine arrangements, as the expression "the Qur'an" indicates, He added to the challenge the condition of gathering together of both the two weights (al-thaqalan: mankind and jinn); and He turned the aspirations toward mutual support, cooperation, and combined effort, unlike what passed in the earlier surahs. So He said (Exalted is He), emphasizing with the lam that prepares for an oath (al-lam al-muwatta'ah li'l-qasam), because of their claim that if they willed they could bring the like of it, and the response is then to the oath, while the response of the condition is omitted, indicated by the response of the oath: ﴿Truly, if mankind and the jinn gathered together﴾ — those whom you know, and you know what they have brought of eloquence and wisdom — and those whom you do not know; and He put them first for the ease of their gathering with one another, and because they are, in their view, the origin of eloquence; ﴿and the jinn﴾ — those who come to your soothsayers, encourage them, and inform them of some of the unseen matters that are hidden from them; (p-509) and He left out the angels because they have no familiarity with any of their speech; ﴿on the condition that they would bring﴾ — that is, that they would renew the bringing of something, at some time, while gathered together; ﴿the like of this Qur'an﴾ — that is, all of it, in the form it is in, with its detail; and He singled it out with the demonstrative to alert that what he (ﷺ) says from Allah is revelation from Allah, in which there is nothing of his own self; and that what is meant in this context of the challenge, the one whose name is the Qur'an, is specifically this; ﴿they would not bring﴾.

And since this surah is Meccan, and the most that this verse can be is the last of the Meccan [revelation], the challenge is restricted to it. And when the apparent noun is repeated as a pronoun, the specificity becomes possible, whereas what is intended is generality; and when generality is intended, it is resumed with a noun, encompassing it by resuming an encompassing apparent noun, as al-Harrali mentions at the end of surah "al-Kahf." He did not say here "like it" (bihi), for this reason, and so that it would not be thought that it refers to the Qur'an and not to its like; rather he made it apparent, and said — indicating that what is meant is all of the Meccan and the Medinan — ﴿like it﴾: that is, not with restriction to its true and wise meanings, so that they would bring speech at the highest levels of eloquence, clarifying the finest meanings with the clearest structures; nor with deviation from them toward invented meanings. Then he clarified that the judgment is that of their inability, whether gathered together, or alone, or supporting one another, or not supporting one another. So He said (Exalted is He): ﴿And even if﴾ — and since the responsible ones are naturally inclined to opposition and conflicting aims (p-510) — He said (Exalted is He): ﴿they were﴾ — that is, by natural disposition and custom, contrary to the usual — ﴿some of them to others a helper﴾ — that is, supporting, by combining the strongest of what is in one with the strongest of what is in his companion. And what completes this meaning has already been mentioned in the surahs in which the challenge occurs.

Now that these sentences have been completed in this beautiful manner and with this sublime description, He, glory be to Him, drew attention to this by His saying, coordinating it with the phrase, "We have turned these parables about as you see, on the highest method, with the most eloquent arrangement, in the most wondrous order": ﴿And We have certainly turned about for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾. That is, We repeated and reiterated them many times, by the greatness that is Ours. Since the foundation of the surah is the explanation of the care given to people who have taqwa and who are doers of good, the context required, for greater emphasis, placing His saying ﴿for the people﴾ first. That is, those who are human beings. ﴿in this Qur'an﴾, which guides to what is most upright, ﴿every kind of example﴾. That is, every example that is, in its strangeness, its circulation throughout the regions of the earth, its eloquence, its clarity, and its elegance, like the example that must be taken as a lesson. And "tasrif" (turning about, the variation of expression) is making the meaning revolve in different directions, by means of the annexed term, the attribute, the relative clause, and the like. ﴿But most people refused﴾. That is, as a consequence of that which is the cause of healing, thankfulness, and guidance, in confirmation of Our saying: ﴿And it does not increase the wrongdoers except in loss﴾, they refused (p-511) ﴿most people﴾, and they are who they are, in the form of people, while their meanings have been stripped away.

Since "refused" (abā) is interpreted (ta'wil) with the meaning of negation, so the meaning becomes: they did not accept, along with arrogance and aversion, He received it with the particle of "istithna'" (exception), and said, ﴿except disbelief﴾, because of the turmoil that they are in.

Since this was a matter that caused wonder, He expressed amazement at them in another way, linking it by conjunction to "and they ask you" (if by "people" in His saying "but most of the people refused" is meant all of them), or to "but refused" (if by them is meant Quraysh). So He said (Exalted is He): ﴿And they said﴾; that is, the disbelievers of Quraysh and those who allied with them, out of obstinacy, after the proof had become binding upon them by the demonstration of their inability to produce its like, and for other reasons, acting like one who is struck dumb, overcome by proof, and stubborn, emphasizing what the proof had made binding upon them, by which they had come to be among those who believe with certainty without hesitation: ﴿We will not believe﴾; that is, we will not affirm what you say, submitting, ﴿in you until you cause to gush forth﴾; that is, a great gushing, ﴿for us﴾; that is, all of us, ﴿from the earth a spring﴾; that is, a spring whose water never runs dry.

Or you should have a garden of palm trees and grapevines, and cause rivers to gush forth within it in abundant flow. (Note: the translation below follows the text.)

Let me correct that and give the translation exactly as the passage stands:

"Or that you should have a garden of palm trees and grapes" — ﴿أوْ تَكُونَ لَكَ﴾: meaning, you alone; "a garden of palm trees and [of] grape-vines" — he expressed it by the fruit (ʿinab, grapes) because benefit from it apart from fruit is little; ﴿so that you cause to gush forth﴾: meaning, with an additional magnificence; ﴿the rivers﴾: flowing; ﴿within it in a gushing﴾: and it is a splitting of what flows of water, or light, or the like of them. So "al-fajr" (dawn-break, al-fajr): the splitting of darkness at the column of dawn; and "al-fujur" (wickedness, al-fujur): (p-512) the tearing of the cloak of modesty, with what leads to corruption.

﴿Or cause the sky to fall upon us in pieces﴾, i.e., the sky itself, ﴿as you claimed﴾ regarding what you threaten us with. ﴿Pieces﴾, i.e., fragments, the plural of "kisfah" (كِسْفَةٌ), which is a single piece. It is also possible that what is meant is the stone-storm (al-ḥāṣib) coming from above, and other punishments they were warned of, as in His saying, "that He may send upon you a punishment from above you" (﴿أَنْ يَبْعَثَ عَلَيْكُمْ عَذَابًا مِنْ فَوْقِكُمْ﴾). Calling that "sky" is like calling rain, and even plants, "sky":

"When the sky descends upon a people's land,
we graze upon it, even if they are angry."

﴿Or you bring God﴾, i.e., the Supreme King, ﴿and the angels, face to face﴾, i.e., coming in visible presence and confrontation, looked upon, such that nothing of Him is hidden from any one of us. Its original sense is gathering, which necessarily entails facing one another with approach, from the "qabā'il al-ra's" (قَبائِلِ الرَّأْسِ), the gathering parts of the head.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 93:

﴿Or you have a house of gold⦗zukhruf⦘﴾; that is, особенно for you; ﴿a house of ornament﴾; that is, of gold; complete in beauty and adornment; ﴿or you ascend⦗tarqa⦘﴾; that is, rise; ﴿into the sky﴾; step by step; while we watch you ascending; ﴿and we will not believe⦗nu'min⦘﴾; that is, we will not affirm with submission; ﴿for your ascent⦗ruqiyyika⦘﴾; that is, at all; ﴿until you bring down⦗tunazzilu⦘﴾; and they confirmed the meaning of its coming from heaven by their saying: ﴿a book upon us﴾; and the meaning of its being on parchment, or something similar to their saying, by their saying: ﴿that we may read it﴾; in which it commands us to follow you.

When their obstinacy was complete, and the tongue of the situation was asking God (Exalted) for the answer to it, God (Exalted) commanded him to answer them by His saying: ﴿Say: Glory be to my Lord﴾; that is, exalted is He above having a partner in His dominion who asks of Him what is asked only of God. It is therefore a declaration of God's transcendence, and an expression of wonder at them, given the clarity of their obstinacy in demanding what no one has power over except God, from one who has no power over any part of it except by God's permission. He never claimed that he had power over any part of it. Thus the interrogative in His saying (Exalted): ﴿Am I anything but a human messenger?⦗basharan rasulan⦘﴾ is most fitting: he has power over nothing beyond what humans have power over, ﴿a messenger⦗rasulan⦘﴾ like the messengers before me. I do not exceed what I was commanded regarding conveying the message; so I bring nothing except by God's permission. I did not say, "I am a god," so that what is asked of a god should be asked of me. They arranged themselves in this order because they restricted his state to a claim that he be great by prophethood or by something else, so that people would follow him. If it is the first, he would be one whose word is accepted by the One who sent him; and then either they would ask him for a general benefit, a spring of water, or for something specific to him, a garden, if he withheld the general benefit; or for harm, pieces of the sky falling; or they would ask him to come with his troops so that they would believe him. And if his greatness were by other than this, then either he would be a king, so that he would have the house mentioned, as is customary for one who has followers; or he would be one who meets with the king who sent him and so ascends, as they said.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 94:

When He had commanded what implies that he (the Prophet) is, like his brethren among the Messengers, a human being, He followed it with His saying (exalted is He), in conjunction with "fa-abā" (but he refused) or "fa-qālū" (so they said): ﴿And nothing prevented the people﴾; that is, Quraysh, and whoever said what they said, due to the confusion they were in; ﴿from believing﴾; that is, no barrier remained for them from faith; and the clause is the object of "prevented"; ﴿when guidance had come to them﴾; that is, the decisive proof for faith, which is the Qur'an and other proofs; ﴿except﴾; and the subject of "prevented" is ﴿that they said﴾; that is, denying in the utmost degree of denial, astonished, mocking: ﴿"Has God sent a human being as a messenger?"﴾; that is, with His dazzling greatness and the attributes of majesty and honour; ﴿a human being as a messenger﴾. And the cause of following misguidance, despite its evident harm, and of abandoning guidance, despite its manifest benefit, is the occurrence of doubt or desire to weak-minded people, who are most people, at the beginning; then the imitation of leaders; and then the settling of bad custom after that.

When they denied that the Messenger was a human being, after they had made a stone into a god, He taught him their answer through His saying (Exalted is He): ﴿Say﴾ to them: My Lord, glory be to Him and exalted is He, said: ﴿Had there been﴾, i.e., settled presence, ﴿in the earth﴾, which is the dwelling place of the children of Adam, ﴿angels walking﴾ upon it as the children of Adam do, without flying as the angels fly to the heaven, ﴿at rest﴾, having taken it as a settled abode, as humans have done, ﴿We would have sent down﴾, i.e., with the greatness that is ours, ﴿upon them﴾ time after time, as We did in sending down Jibril, peace be upon him, upon the prophets from among humans. He confirmed the matter by His saying (Exalted is He): ﴿from the heaven an angel as a messenger﴾, because they are able to receive from him, being of the same kind as them, unlike (p-515) humans, as the requirement of wisdom demands, since the messenger of every kind should be from among them, for a thing is better understood from its own form, is more familiar with it, better suited to it, and more attached to it. Except for one whom He has favored by making his soul and intellect dominant over his desire, thereby empowering him to receive from the angel.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 96:

When He had established the decisive proof that the Qur'an revealed to him is from Allah, and had negated their doubt about denying that the Messenger was a human being, by [showing] that he did not depart from the custom of those before him, among those who used to acknowledge that they were prophets; and by [showing] that one kind does not comprehend from another kind; so a human being cannot comprehend from an angel except by means of a miraculous sign (khariqah); and that this is not granted except to the messengers, and to whomever of their followers Allah wills; nothing remained but pure obstinacy, which admits of no return except to the sword when one has the power, and to Allah when that power is lacking. He was in Makkah the Honored, unable to use the sword, so Allah (Exalted) commanded him to return to the sword. Thus He (Exalted) said: ﴿Say: Allah suffices as a witness﴾; that is, the One who encompasses everything in power and knowledge; ﴿as a witness﴾; that is, a decider who will be ﴿between me and you﴾, dealing with each of us according to what he deserves. Then He gave the reason for His sufficiency in that by His saying (Exalted): ﴿Indeed, He is ever, of His servants, Acquainted and Seeing﴾; ﴿Acquainted﴾ before He created them, with what their affair would come to after bringing them into existence; ﴿Seeing﴾ with what would proceed from them after their existence.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 97:

Since it has been established that He, glorified and exalted, knows best who is guided and who is astray, and since the conclusion of this verse points to the meaning that whoever He knows to have a receptiveness to good in his response, He enables him to act in accordance with that (musha-kalah: congruence of the outcome with the disposition), and whoever He knows to have a receptiveness to evil, He leaves astray, He follows it with His saying, exalted be He: ﴿And whoever Allah guides﴾ (p-٥١٦); that is, He to whom all command belongs, because He has no partner, by creating guidance in his heart. He indicated the scarcity of the guided, in the manner of excellence, by using a singular pronoun, and the abundance of the astray by using the plural. So He, exalted be He, said: ﴿then he is the one guided﴾ [al-Kahf: 17]; that is, not anyone else. No one other than Him can cause him to go astray. ﴿And whoever He leaves astray﴾: then he is the one astray, with no guide for him. This is the meaning of His saying, exalted be He: ﴿you will not find for them allies﴾; that is, for those who are astray, ﴿supporters﴾, that is, helpers in this world, ﴿besides Him﴾ [al-A'raf: 197]; who could guide them, and who could benefit them in anything that God has willed otherwise. For this reason they are negated in principle and entirely, because if their benefit is negated, they are as nothing. And if it is negated for the plural, it is negated for the singular a fortiori. So the verse is an instance of ihtibak (a device in which two contrasting elements are mentioned and each one's counterpart is left implicit): the statement about the first implies the omission of its opposite in the second, and the result of the second implies the omission of its opposite from the first.

When the Day of Judgment, the Day of Decision, is the day on which there appears to each and every person, in every state, of the greatness of His, exalted be He, [greatness] which causes all other greatness to vanish, He said: ﴿And We will gather them﴾ with the plural of majesty; that is, We will assemble them by compulsion, ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾; that is, the day which is the seat of wisdom, ﴿upon their faces﴾, walking, or being dragged upon them, as humiliation for them therein, just as they did not humble them through prostration to Us; ﴿blind, mute and deaf﴾, just as they were in the world, not benefiting from their sight, their speech, or their hearing, but rather it becomes a harm to them, because of what they look upon of destructions, what they hear of calamities, and what they utter of faults. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': when a person is gathered upon what he died upon, nothing will be for him in the Hereafter except that its beginning and origin have occurred in this world, and its completion in the Hereafter, end of quote.

Since the context calls for a transition from one station to another, he put sight first, because it is the principal thing in that. He followed it with speech, because the blind can still seek guidance, and he concluded with hearing, because with hearing alone some kind of guidance is possible. If the conjunction (waw) [joining them] is for combining all of them in each of the attributes, then it serves tahwil (intensification of the terror); because when the speaker utters the conjunction, the listener thinks he is moving to something else, and then when he gives the description it becomes more striking, since it is known that its bearer is well-versed in it, as was mentioned in "Bara'a" (the title of surah 9). If the conjunction is for tanwi' (variation), then it is to depict them in the most ugly form, in that one group among them benefits the other not at all. It is as if it was said: "To what place are they gathered?" So He, exalted be He, said: ﴿Their refuge is Hell﴾; it blazes over them and scowls at them. Each one of them suffers its punishment alone, even if his face is turned toward the face of his companion, because he perceives nothing but the punishment, due to the sealing of his faculties. How long is its exile! And how great is its distress! It is as if it was said: "Will its punishment be abated for them?" So it was said: "No; rather they are increasing every moment," because ﴿whenever it subsides﴾; that is, its flame begins to die down when it cooks their skins, ﴿We increase them﴾; that is, by what We have of majesty, ﴿in blaze﴾, by renewing the skins.

Then he explained the reason for their punishment, so that whoever among them had been decreed happiness might return. So He (Exalted) said: ﴿That﴾, i.e., the great punishment, ﴿is their recompense because they﴾, the people of misguidance, ﴿disbelieved in Our signs﴾ (p-518) of the Qur'an and others, along with their great standing in being attributed to Us; and they were increasing in disbelief every day, and they were resolved to persist in that for as long as they lived. ﴿And they said﴾, denying Our power: ﴿When we are bones and crumbled remains?﴾, scattered in the earth. Then they repeated the denial, as if they were confident in this matter of theirs, whose falsehood is clearer than the sun, by saying: ﴿Shall we indeed be resurrected in a new creation?﴾, i.e., is our resurrection established? So We show them, as a recompense for this repeated denial, a new creation in their skins, renewed every moment: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted through, We replace them with other skins, that they may taste the punishment﴾ [an-Nisa: 56].

Then He followed it with a decisive statement explaining their ignorance. He said, alerting that they are more deserving of denial, and linking it to what is implied: "Have they not seen that God, who originated their creation, is able to restore them" (the implied clause being supplied): ﴿Have they not seen﴾; that is, they should know with the eyes of their insight, a knowledge that is like seeing with the eyes of their sight, because of the proofs it rests upon and the majestic evidences that proclaim its soundness; ﴿that God﴾; that is, the Sovereign Most High, encompassing everything in power and knowledge, none other than Him; ﴿who created the heavens﴾; He gathered them together because of the beauty that indicates this; and since the earth does not have a similar description, He made it singular, intending the kind of noun suited to collective use. So He said (exalted is He): ﴿and the earth﴾; despite the greatness of its bodies, the magnitude of its firmness, the strength of its parts, the vastness of its expanses, and the abundance of conveniences and aids in it, which He tears apart and annihilates, then renews and brings to life again; ﴿is able to create﴾; that is, to renew at whatever time He wills; ﴿their like﴾; at the beginning. So how much more so the restoration? And they are weaker in matter and lower in status. ﴿And﴾ that He; ﴿appointed for them a term﴾; for their punishment, or their death, or their resurrection, because it is known in itself; ﴿there is no doubt in it﴾; in any way whatsoever; because they have repeatedly witnessed that a soul is not delayed when its term comes, and likewise is not advanced beyond its term. How many have men of the lions, the brave champions and the stallion-men, striven to harm him or to kill him, while they were certain that he was in their grip, yet they were unable to do so; then it happened by the weakest of people or by the feeblest cause. Thus it becomes known that He alone has the power to originate and to annihilate. ﴿But refused﴾; that is, rather; they knew this with a knowledge like the sensed and seen; yet from that cause for belief there resulted their refusal. This is how the original order would be; but He manifested it in a general form and tied it to a description, so He said: ﴿the wrongdoers﴾; that is, these obstinate ones refused because of their wrongdoing; ﴿except disbelief﴾; that is, denial, because of not associating [anything with Him].

ولَمّا قَدَّمَ في هَذِهِ السُّورَةِ أنَّهُ هو المُعْطِي؛ وأنَّ عَطاءَهُ الجَمَّ - الَّذِي فاتَ الحَصْرَ؛ وفَضَلَ عَنِ الحاجَةِ؛ وقامَتْ بِهِ الحُجَّةُ عَلى العِبادِ في تَمامِ قُدْرَتِهِ؛ وكَمالِ عِلْمِهِ - غَيْرُ مَحْظُورٍ عَنْ أحَدٍ؛ وأنَّهم يَقْتُلُونَ أوْلادَهُمْ؛ مَعَ ذَلِكَ؛ خَشْيَةَ الإمْلاقِ؛ وهم يَطْلُبُونَ أنْ يَظْهَرَ لَهم مِن جِنْسِ ما خَلَقَ مِنَ اليَنابِيعِ؛ والجَنّاتِ؛ والذَّهَبِ؛ والزُّخْرُفِ؛ عَلى كَيْفِيّاتٍ مَخْصُوصَةٍ؛ لِغَيْرِ حاجَةِ ما تَقَدَّمَ ذِكْرُهُ؛ وقَدِ امْتَنَعُوا بُخْلًا؛ وأنَفَةً؛ وجَهْلًا عَنْ الِاعْتِرافِ لَهُ بِما أوْجَبَهُ عَلَيْهِمْ؛ شُكْرًا لِنِعْمَتِهِ؛ واسْتِدْفاعًا لِنِقْمَتِهِ؛ بَعْدَ قِيامِ الدَّلائِلِ؛ وزَوالِ (p-٥٢٠) الشُّبَهِ؛ فَلا أبْخَلَ مِنهُمْ؛ لِأنَّهم بَخِلُوا مِمّا يَجِبُ عَلَيْهِمْ مِنَ الكَلامِ؛ كَما قالَ النَّبِيُّ (ﷺ): "أبْخَلُ النّاسِ مَن بَخِلَ بِالسَّلامِ"؛ أمَرَهُ أنْ يُنَبِّهَهم عَلى سَفَهِهِمْ في ذَلِكَ؛ بِقَوْلِهِ (تَعالى): ﴿قُلْ لَوْ﴾؛ ولَمّا كانَ مِن حَقِّ "لَوْ"؛ الدُّخُولُ عَلى الأفْعالِ؛ عُلِمَ أنَّ بَعْدَها فِعْلًا مِن جِنْسِ ما بَعْدُ؛ تَقْدِيرُهُ: "تَمْلِكُونَ"؛ ولَكِنَّهُ حَذَفَهُ؛ وفَصَلَ الضَّمِيرَ؛ لِأنَّ المَقْصُودَ الحُكْمُ عَلَيْهِمْ بادِئَ بَدْءٍ؛ فَقالَ (تَعالى): ﴿أنْتُمْ﴾؛ أيْ: دُونَ غَيْرِكُمْ؛ ﴿تَمْلِكُونَ خَزائِنَ﴾؛ عَبَّرَ بِصِيغَةِ مُنْتَهى الجُمُوعِ؛ لِأنَّ المَقامَ جَدِيرٌ بِالمُبالَغَةِ؛ ﴿رَحْمَةِ﴾؛ أيْ: إرْزاقَ؛ وإكْرامَ؛ ﴿رَبِّي﴾؛ المُحْسِنِ إلَيَّ بِإيتائِي جَمِيعَ ما ثَبَّتَ أمْرِي؛ وأوْضَحَهُ؛ وهي مَقْدُوراتُهُ الَّتِي يَرْحَمُ بِها عِبادَهُ؛ بِإضافَتِها عَلَيْهِمْ؛ ﴿إذًا لأمْسَكْتُمْ﴾؛ أيْ: لَوَقَعَ مِنكُمُ الإمْساكُ عَنِ الإنْفاقِ في بَعْضِ الوُجُوهِ الَّتِي تَحْتاجُونَها؛ ﴿خَشْيَةَ﴾؛ عاقِبَةِ ﴿الإنْفاقِ﴾؛ أيْ: المُوصِلِ إلى الفَقْرِ؛ ثُمَّ اسْتَدَلَّ عَلى صِحَّةِ هَذا المَفْرُوضِ بِالمُشاهَدِ مِن مَضْمُونِ قَوْلِهِ (تَعالى): ﴿وكانَ﴾؛ أيْ: جِبِلَّةً وطَبْعًا؛ ﴿الإنْسانُ﴾؛ أيْ: الَّذِي مِن شَأْنِهِ الأنَسُ بِنَفْسِهِ؛ فَهو لِذَلِكَ لا يَعْقِلُ الأُمُورَ حَقَّ عَقْلِها؛ ﴿قَتُورًا﴾؛ أيْ: بَخِيلًا مُمْسِكًا غايَةَ الإمْساكِ؛ لِإمْكانِ أنْ يَكُونَ فَقِيرًا؛ فَلا تَراهُ إلّا مُضَيِّقًا في النَّفَقَةِ عَلى نَفْسِهِ؛ ومَن (p-٥٢١) تَلْزَمُهُ نَفَقَتُهُ؛ شَدِيدًا في ذَلِكَ؛ وإنِ اتَّسَعَتْ أحْوالُهُ؛ وزادَتْ عَلى الحَدِّ أمْوالُهُ؛ لِما فِيهِ مِن صِفَةِ النَّقْصِ اللّازِمَةِ بِلُزُومِ الحاجَةِ لَهُ؛ طُبِعَ عَلى ذَلِكَ؛ فَهو في غَرِيزَتِهِ بِالقُوَّةِ؛ فَكُلُّهم يَفْعَلُهُ؛ إلّا مَن وفَّقَهُ اللَّهُ (تَعالى)؛ فَغَلَبَ عَقْلُهُ عَلى هَواهُ؛ وقَلِيلٌ ما هُمْ؛ أيْ: فَإذا كانَ هَذا أمْرَكم فِيما تَمْلِكُونَهُ؛ مَعَ الحاجَةِ إلى الوُجُوهِ المُنْفَقِ فِيها؛ فَكَيْفَ تَطْلُبُونَ مِنَ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ) ما لا يَمْلِكُهُ؛ ولا ادَّعى القُدْرَةَ عَلَيْهِ؛ أوْ مِنَ الخالِقِ الحَكِيمِ أنْ يَفْعَلَ ما تَتَعَنَّتُونَ بِهِ؛ عَبَثًا بِغَيْرِ حاجَةٍ أصْلًا؟! لِأنَّهُ إنْ كانَ لِإثْباتِ قُدْرَتِهِ فَأنْتُمْ لا تَمْتَرُونَ فِيها؛ وإنْ كانَ لِإثْباتِ رِسالَةِ نَبِيِّكُمْ؛ فَقَدْ ثَبَتَ بِأُمُورٍ - أعْظَمُها هَذا القُرْآنُ الَّذِي مَرَّ آنِفًا - إقامَةُ الدَّلِيلِ عَلَيْها بِهِ؛ وهَتْكُ أسْتارِ شُبْهَتِكم في اسْتِبْعادِ كَوْنِ الرَّسُولِ بَشَرًا؛ واللَّهُ (تَعالى) قَدْ أكْرَمَكم بِنَبِيِّكم عَنْ أنْ يُعاجِلَكم بِالِاسْتِئْصالِ عِنْدَ العِصْيانِ؛ بَعْدَ كَشْفِ الغِطاءِ؛ كَما جَرَتْ بِهِ سُنَّتُهُ في جَمِيعِ الأُمَمِ؛ وإنْ كانَ لِإثْباتِ غِناكم فَهو شَيْءٌ لا يُغْنِي نُفُوسَكُمْ؛ فَيَرُدَّها عَنْ طَلَبِ المَزِيدِ؛ وعَنِ التَّقْتِيرِ؛ لِما طُبِعْتُمْ عَلَيْهِ؛ بَلْ تَكُونُونَ عِنْدَ حُصُولِ ذَلِكَ لَكُمْ؛ لِحُصُولِ الغِنى؛ كالمُسْتَجِيرِ مِنَ الرَّمْضاءِ بِالنّارِ؛ وهو قَدْ قَضى أنَّهُ يَظْهَرُ أمْرُهُ عَلى كُلِّ مَن ناوَأهُ؛ وإنْ كَرِهَ الكافِرُونَ؛ وقَدْ عَلِمَ مَن يُؤْمِنُ؛ فَيُيَسِّرُ لَهُ الإيمانَ؛ ويَجْعَلُهُ (p-٥٢٢) عَوْنًا لِحِزْبِ الرَّحْمَنِ؛ ومَن لا يُؤْمِنُ فَهو يَجْعَلُهُ مَعَ أوْلِياءِ الشَّيْطانِ؛ ويُذِيقُ الكُلَّ الهَوانَ؛ ويَجْعَلُهم وقُودًا لِلنِّيرانِ؛ فَلَمْ يَبْقَ بَعْدَ هَذا كُلِّهِ في إجابَتِكم إلى تَعَنُّتِكم إلّا العَبَثُ؛ الَّذِي هو - سُبْحانَهُ - مُتَعالٍ عَنْهُ؛ فَلا وجْهَ يُحَصِّلُ بِهِ الإنْسانُ الغِنى إلّا اتِّباعُ السُّنَّةِ (sunnah: the Prophet's way and practice)؛ والِانْسِلاخُ عَنِ الهَوى؛ فَمَن وصَلَ إلى ذَلِكَ اسْتَوى عِنْدَهُ الذَّهَبُ والحَصْباءُ.

Al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 17, verse 101:

When He (glorified is He) had mentioned that most people denied the signs, because He had judged them to be astray, and whoever He judges to be astray cannot be guided, and He concluded that whoever is created with a disposition toward something will not part from it, He began to console His Prophet (peace be upon him) with what befell the prophets, his brethren, before him. At the same time, He alerted that He grants signs according to what is required, and that extraordinary events (khawariq al-'adat, miraculous events that break customary patterns) do not benefit the faith of those whom He has judged to be astray, and that, as in God's way (sunnah), they necessitate the destruction of whoever disobeys after them with the punishment of total annihilation (isti'sal). So He said, connecting it to His words: ﴿And We had certainly shown the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾ [al-Isra': 89]: ﴿And We certainly gave﴾, that is, by the greatness We possess, ﴿Moses﴾, the son of 'Imran, the God-fearing, the good-doer (peace be upon him), when We sent him to Pharaoh, ﴿nine clear signs﴾. These are, as in the Torah: the staff; then blood; then frogs; then lice; then the death of livestock; then hail, the large hailstones that God sent along with a blazing fire, which destroyed everything it passed over, of vegetation and animals; then locusts; then darkness; then the death of the firstborn of humans and of all animals. This has already passed in this book, from the Torah, in Surat al-A'raf. It seems that he counted the hand along with the staff as one sign, and did not list the hand separately, because it caused them no harm. I have arranged them in verse so that they are easy to memorize, saying:

"Staff, lice, death of livestock, darkness,
locusts, blood, then frogs and hail."

"And the death of the firstborn of humans and of others,
of the living, He who is mighty and unique brought them."

These are summarized in the Psalms (Zabur), for he said in the seventy-seventh Psalm: "He worked His signs and His wonders in the fields of Zoan. He turned their rivers into blood, and their streams, so that they could not drink. He sent among them swarms of flies, which devoured them, and frogs, which destroyed them. He gave their crops to the caterpillar, and their labor to the locust. He destroyed their vines with hail, and their sycamore trees with frost. He delivered their cattle to the hail, and their flocks to fiery bolts. He sent upon them the fierceness of His anger, wrath, indignation and trouble, a band of destroying angels. He made a path for His anger; He did not spare their souls from death, but gave their lives over to the plague. He smote all the firstborn in Egypt, the first-fruits of their strength in the tents of Ham."

He also said in the one hundred and fourth Psalm, after mentioning God's works among the children of Israel and their fathers: "He called for a famine upon the land and destroyed all the staff of bread. He sent a man before them, Joseph, who was sold as a slave. They hurt his feet with fetters; he was laid in iron until the time that his word came to pass, and the word of the Lord tested him. The king sent and loosed him; the ruler of the people let him go free. He made him lord of his house and ruler of all his possessions, to bind his princes at his pleasure and teach his elders wisdom. Israel also came into Egypt, and Jacob sojourned in the land of Ham. He increased His people greatly and made them stronger than their enemies. He turned their hearts to hate His people and to deal subtly with His servants. He sent Moses His servant, and Aaron whom He had chosen. They performed His signs among them and wonders in the land of Ham. He sent darkness and made it dark, and they did not rebel against His words. He turned their waters into blood and killed their fish. Their land brought forth frogs, even in the chambers of their kings. He spoke, and there came swarms of flies and lice in all their borders. He gave them hail for rain, and fire burning in their land. He smote their vines and their fig trees, and broke the trees of their country. He spoke, and the locusts came, and caterpillars without number, and they ate up every herb in their land and devoured the fruit of their ground. He smote also all the firstborn in their land, the chief of all their strength."

However, the Psalm does not mention the staff. This may be because of its great fame among them, and because all the signs were performed by means of it. Thus it is in reality the comprehensive sign encompassing all the others. I have said that these are the signs because the context indicates that Pharaoh saw them all and persisted in obstinacy after seeing them. This is an indication that even if He gave the disbelievers of Quraysh what they proposed, such as making a spring gush forth and what accompanies it, it would not restrain them from stubbornness. So bringing it would be pointless, with no benefit in it.

Since the Jews, who instructed Quraysh to ask the Prophet (may God bless him and his family and grant them peace) about the Spirit (the answer to which has already been given, as in some narrations), and about the People of the Cave and Dhu al-Qarnayn (whose stories will be explained in Surat al-Kahf), He alerted them, if they would accept their word, to the matter of Moses (peace be upon him): that he, like this noble Prophet, was a human being while also being a messenger, and that he brought extraordinary signs, which the stubborn ones denied, so the denier was uprooted. He said (exalted is He): ﴿So ask﴾, that is, O greatest of Our creation, ﴿the Children of Israel﴾, that is, in general, those who alerted Quraysh about the matter of the Spirit, concerning the account of Moses (peace be upon him), or the believers, such as 'Abdullah ibn Salam and his companions. ﴿When﴾, that is, concerning that, ﴿he came to them﴾, that is, came to their fathers, and there befell him from denial after the manifestation of the astonishing miracles what befell you. He was not denied because of a flaw in his affair, nor because of strength on the part of his enemy to resist the punishment. Rather it was ignorance and obstinacy, so that this would be a consolation for you and a sign of the corruption of their natures, and a decisive proof against them. ﴿Then he said﴾, that is, then he went to Pharaoh and commanded him to send them with him. He refused, so Moses showed him the signs one after another. As a result, the opposite of what the situation required occurred: ﴿Pharaoh said to him﴾, out of arrogance and haughtiness: ﴿I certainly think you﴾ (he emphasized his statement because of what Moses (peace be upon him) had shown, which required submission to him and belief, and rejecting that anyone should deny him), ﴿O Moses, to be bewitched﴾, that is, everything that comes from you is one of the effects of the magic that is in you, an imagination with no reality, and you in reality are bewitched, and because magic exists in you there is a magician. Abu 'Ubayd said: as one says "maymun" meaning "yamin" (blessed, in the sense of one who is fortunate). It seems he was deceiving his soldiers when he showed them the sign of the hand, with this doubt. This is like what Quraysh said: ﴿You follow only a man bewitched﴾ [al-Isra': 47], and in another place they said: "a magician." They sometimes use the passive form while meaning the active, as an exaggeration that he is like one compelled to act. In the command to ask the Jews there is an alert to their misguidance. Shaykh Wali al-Din al-Malawi said: Perhaps from this derives the scholars' practice in debate of demanding that Jews and Christians and others prove the prophethood of their prophets. Every method they follow is followed in establishing the prophethood of Muhammad (may God bless him and his family and grant them peace), and every objection they raise is raised against them in the same way. Whatever is a reply to them is a reply for us. Whoever attends closely to this noble verse will see in it something wondrous. End of quotation. Yet Pharaoh did not believe, despite the succession of those signs and their magnitude.

Then it is as if it were said: "What did Moses (peace be upon him) say?" It was said: ﴿He said﴾ to Pharaoh: "Indeed you know" — i.e., I [know], with a damma on the ta' (tā'), according to the reading of al-Kisā'ī, to convey that he has certain knowledge that what he brought is sent down from his Lord, so he is the most intelligent person of that age; and it is not as Pharaoh claimed. Or with a fatḥa on the ta' (tā'), according to the reading of the rest of the readers, meaning: "You, O Pharaoh, by what I have manifested of the proofs, have become among those who know that ﴿He sent down﴾ — through my hands — ﴿these﴾ signs ﴿but the Lord of the heavens and the earth﴾, i.e., their Creator and their Sustainer, while these signs are ﴿insights﴾, i.e., clear evidences, their matter being firm and their worth exalted, by which my truthfulness is seen. As for magic, it is not hidden from anyone that it is imagination without any reality. ﴿And indeed I﴾, i.e., even if you, O Pharaoh, think me ﴿bewitched﴾, ﴿I surely think you﴾ — emphasized because of those with Pharaoh who deny his words and display certainty about Pharaoh's happiness — ﴿O Pharaoh, doomed﴾, i.e., cursed, driven away, defeated, destroyed, deprived of good, corrupt in intellect. My assumption is close to correctness, unlike your assumption, due to your obstinacy toward the Lord of the worlds and the clear evidence of your denial of the insights by which the veil was lifted; they are clearer than the sun. This is because of your inclination toward the state in which you are, and your laziness in moving away from it toward what is more noble. I have explained the root meaning of "ثبر" (thabar) in "lā tathrība" (no reproach) in Surat Yusuf (peace be upon him); if you review it, what I have pointed to will become clear to you.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 17, verse 103:

﴿So he intended﴾; that is: what resulted from this, which is ordinarily the requirement of faith, was not so; rather, Pharaoh intended ﴿to drive them out﴾; that is: to frighten Musa and those who believed with him (istikhaf), and to expel them, so that they would be like water when it flows, from their saying "fazza al-jurh" (the wound flowed); ﴿from the land﴾; by banishment and killing, so that he could be firmly in control of enslaving the rest; just as these people intended to drive you out from the land, so that they could expel you from it, in order to be firmly established in their disbelief and obstinacy. Then He began to warn them of His might by what He did to those who were more numerous than them and mightier, so He said: ﴿Then We drowned him﴾; that is: as a consequence of that, We turned back his scheme against his own throat, with the greatness that is ours, so We did not let him attain his aim; and We provoked him ourselves, so he could not refrain, but rushed on without knowing what We intended for him, until We brought him into the sea, where We had brought the Children of Israel; so We saved them and drowned him, ﴿and those with him, all of them﴾; as Our custom has been with whoever opposed after (p-529) having seen the marvels, disbelieved the blessing, and exceeded in transgression after the truth had become manifest. So let these people beware of the like of that, especially if We expel Our Messenger from among them. Thus in this verse and its like there is good news for him of Our placing him, in victory and establishment, on the path of his brother messengers, peace be upon them.

And We said: that is, by the majesty We possess, which nothing can exceed in greatness.

Since this saying does not encompass the whole time after the drowning, He (exalted is He) affirmed the preposition, saying: ﴿after him﴾, that is, after the drowning, ﴿to the Children of Israel﴾, who were under his hand, more abject than slaves, on account of their piety and their good deeds, ﴿Dwell in the land﴾, that is, the land in general. This is an indication that Pharaoh wanted to erase them from the land, or that their dwelling, despite his existence, was as if it did not exist, because of the humiliation they suffered.
